indeed, that man who performs a *śrāddha* at the *śālagrāma* stone [attains them]. (137)
The ancestors of those men who constantly drink the water from the Śālagrāma stone remain satisfied in heaven for a hundred kalpas. (138)
What is the use of consuming thousands of the five products of the cow?
What is the use of visiting thousands of millions of sacred pilgrimage sites? ||139||
If one drinks the meritorious water originating from the body of the Śālagrāma stone,
that place where the Śālagrāma stone is located becomes a sacred pilgrimage site (tīrtha) for three yojanas around.
In that regard, every act of giving and every burnt offering becomes ten millionfold for one who drinks even as much as a single drop of water from the Śālagrāma stone. (141)
Furthermore, that man who partakes of Viṣṇu shall never again drink the breast milk of a mother;
indeed, within a distance of one krośa all around the vicinity of a Śālagrāma stone— ||142||
Even a worm that dies while [touching] the discus-marked stone of Śālagrāma goes to the supreme abode of Vaikuṇṭha; he who gives this as a gift performs the highest charity. (143)
That man who would assign a price to a Śālagrāma stone would not have given away even the entire earth, with its mountains, forests, and groves. (144)
The seller, the one who consents, and he who rejoices in the examinations—all of them go to hell until the dissolution of all beings. (145)
Therefore, one should avoid the buying and selling of a Vaiśya’s trade;
what more need be said, O Vaiśya? One who fears sin must act accordingly. (146)
The remembrance of Vāsudeva, the remover of all sins, is superior to a man who, having restrained his senses, performs severe penance in the forest. (147)
Having bowed to the one whose banner is Garuḍa, a man who, though filled with delusion, has committed many sins, attains that very fruit [of liberation]. (148)
Having gone there, one does not go to hell; for Hari removes all sins.
Whatever holy places and meritorious shrines exist upon the earth, [they are all encompassed by him]. (149)
One attains all of those through the chanting of the names of Viṣṇu—those who have taken refuge in the Lord Viṣṇu, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, as their supreme resort. (150)
They shall not share the world of Yama, nor shall they be dwellers in hell—those Vaiṣṇava men, O Vaiśya, who utter even a single word of censure against Śiva. ||151||
A human being who observes even a single Ekādaśī fast, even by chance, shall indeed go to the realm of Viṣṇu and not to a great hell. (152)
"I have heard from Lomaśa that one does not go to the Yāmya hell;
indeed, nothing so purifying as this exists in the three worlds. (153)
Both [the day and night] of Padmanābha destroy sin;
O best of people, sins dwell here in this body only for that long. (154)
As long as a person does not observe the auspicious day of Padmanābha by fasting, [they miss the merit of] thousands of horse sacrifices and hundreds of Rājasūya sacrifices. (155)
O Vaiśya, the sins committed by men through the eleven senses do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of fasting on the eleventh day. 156.
By fasting on the eleventh day (Ekādaśī), all that [sin] shall go to destruction;
there exists no merit in the world equal to Ekādaśī. (157)
Even those who perform it under a pretext come under the power of the Sun;
indeed, this [vow] bestows heaven and liberation, and grants health to the body. (158)
This [river] bestows a virtuous wife and grants sons who live long;
it is not Gaṅgā, nor Naga, nor Gayā, nor Vaiśya, nor Kāśī, nor Puṣkara. 159.
Nor indeed is a Vaiṣṇava sacred field equal to a day of Hari;
nor are the Yamunā and Candrabhāgā rivers equal to a day of Hari. (160)
By means of which, without effort, the state of Viṣṇu is indeed attained there—having observed a fast on the day of Hari and having kept a vigil at night. (161)
In the paternal lineage of ten ancestors, as well as the maternal lineage of ten ancestors, he certainly uplifts his beloved wife and her ten ancestors to the status of Vaiśyas. 162.
Having abandoned the bonds of duality and made their home in the state of homelessness, those adorned with garlands and clad in yellow robes proceed to the abode of Hari. (163)
O best of the Vaiśyas, whether in childhood, youth, or old age, one who fasts on Ekādaśī certainly does not fall into a miserable state of existence. 164.
Having observed these three-night fasts, performed ablutions at sacred fords,
and given gold, sesame seeds, and cows, men go to heaven.
Those who have not bathed at sacred fords, nor given gold as a gift, nor performed any austerity whatsoever—these shall be miserable everywhere. (166)
The Dharma concerning the description of hell has been briefly explained:
it is non-malice toward all beings through the actions of speech, mind, and body. (167)

The restraint of the senses, the practice of generosity, the service of the virtuous, and the constant protection of the duties of one's caste and stage of life according to the prescribed rules. ||168||
One who desires heaven should never boast of his asceticism or gifts as a Vaiśya;
rather, he should give according to his capacity, desiring his own welfare. 169.
Sandals, clothing, food, a vehicle, roots, fruits, water, shelter, and a dwelling—these should be provided even by a poor man to a Vaiśya on the day of his duty. (170)
Neither in this world nor in the next does what is not given remain with one;
indeed, the givers do not experience those various torments of Yama.
May you be long-lived and wealthy here again and again; what is the use of saying more? Do not go to a miserable rebirth through unrighteousness.
By means of dharma, people ascend to heaven everywhere and at all times. ||173||
Therefore, beginning from the state of a fool, the compendium of dharma must be practiced.
Thus everything has been told to you; what else do you wish to hear? (174)
Vikuṇḍala said:
Having heard your words, O gentle one, my mind has thus become serene; for the speech of the virtuous is an immediate destroyer of sin, like the water of the Gaṅgā which removes all evil. (175)
To help others and speak kindly is the innate quality of the virtuous;
by whom can the cool-rayed moon, the orb of nectar, be made cold? (176)
"O Devadūta, out of compassion, please tell me who am asking you:
how can my brother’s immediate deliverance from hell be brought about? (177)
Having heard these words of his, the divine messenger spoke after gazing into meditation for a moment and reflecting upon him, bound as he was by the rope of friendliness toward him. (178)
Whatever merit you have accumulated through your birth in the eighth Vaiśya caste—all that should be given to your brother, if you desire heaven for him. (179)
Vikuṇḍala said:
What is that merit? How was it produced? What was his former birth? O messenger, let all of that be told; then I shall quickly perform my service. (180)
The divine messenger said:
Listen, O Vaiśya, I shall proclaim that merit along with its cause.
Formerly, in the holy Madhuvana forest, there was a sage named Śākuni. (181)
Endowed with austerity and sacred study, and equal to Brahmā in splendor, nine sons were born to him by Revatī, like the nine planets. (182)
Dhruva, Śīla, Budha, Tāra, and Jyotiṣmat as the fifth—these were devoted to the fire-sacrifice and took delight in the duties of the household life. 183.
Free from delusion, having conquered desire, a treasury of meditation, and preeminent in virtues—these four sons of twice-born men were detached from the household life. (184)
Having entered the fourth stage of life, they were free from desire for all worldly pleasures; though dwelling in a village, they were entirely without attachment and possessed nothing. ||185||
Free from hope and devoid of effort, regarding a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal,
they are clothed in whatever is available and fed by whatever comes their way.
In this way, at evening, the planets were constantly devoted to meditation on Viṣṇu;
they had conquered sleep and conquered their appetite, and they endured wind and cold.
Beholding the entire world, including all that is moving and unmoving, as the form of Viṣṇu, they wander the earth in sport, observing silence toward one another.
For yogis who have realized knowledge and are free from doubt, being experts in the transformations of consciousness, there is no activity whatsoever; they possess only the pure object. 189.
Thus, in his eighth previous birth, that brahmin lived in the Middle Country together with his wife, children, and family.
At midday, thirsty and hungry for sugarcane juice, they came to your house;
at that time, during the interval of the Vaiśvadeva offering, you saw them in the group of houses.
With a faltering voice, eyes filled with tears, and full of joy as well as agitation,
he prostrated himself like a staff, preceded by great reverence.
Having bowed their heads at her feet and joined their palms in reverence,
they were all then greeted by her with words of pleasant truth.
Today my merit has borne fruit, and likewise my birth and life have become fruitful;
today Viṣṇu is pleased with me, and today I am protected and purified. (194)
I am blessed today; my home is blessed; my family is blessed today. My parents are blessed today; my cows are blessed; and the sacred learning I have heard is wealth. (195)
Since your feet, which remove the threefold suffering, have been seen by me, your sight belongs only to one as fortunate as Hari. (196)
Having thus worshipped him and likewise performed the washing of his feet, O best of men, he then placed [the water] upon his head with supreme faith. (197)
O Vaiśya, wherever the water from the feet is placed upon the head with faith, accompanied by perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains, incense, and lamps, preceded by a sincere disposition; ||198||
Having honored them and fed the ascetics with excellent food, they remained there,
fully satisfied, and rested in the palace during the night.
And for those who meditate upon the Supreme Brahman, which is considered the light of lights—the merit arising from their hospitality, O best of men, has been produced by you. (200)
Indeed, even with a thousand faces, I am not able to fully describe this:
among all beings, living creatures are the best; and among living creatures, those who live by their intelligence are the best. (201)
Among the unintelligent, the gods are the best; among men, those born of the Brahmin caste;
among Brahmins, the learned; and among the learned, those whose intellects are devoted to virtuous deeds. (202)

Those who perform actions for those who have attained wisdom, and those who know Brahman for those who perform actions—for this very reason they are highly venerable, and therefore they are the most excellent in the three worlds. (203)
O best of the Vaiśyas, association with them destroys even great sins;
they rest in the home of the householder, contented and knowing Brahman. (204)
It truly destroys in an instant the sin accumulated from birth, as well as whatever sin has been accumulated by a householder until the end of life. (205)
A mendicant who has fasted for a single night completely burns away all that [evil];
give that merit to your brother, so that he may be liberated from hell. (206)
Having heard these words of the messenger, that brother quickly gave the merit with a joyful heart; he too emerged from hell. (207)
Honored by the gods with a rain of flowers, the two departed for heaven;
having been duly honored by them, the messenger returned the way he had come.
Having heard the words of the divine messenger, which brought awakening to the entire world and were equal to the declarations of the Vedas,
the son of the merchant saved his brother by giving away the merit he had himself performed.
He did not go together with him to the excellent world of the Lord of the Gods. ||209||
If a king should read or even hear this history,
he obtains the fruit of the gift of a thousand cows, free from all sorrow.
Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the Svargakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa. ||31||
(32) Chapter Thirty-Two.
Nārada said:
Thence, O king of kings, one should go to Sugandha, renowned throughout the world;
with one's self purified of all sins, one is glorified in the world of Brahmā. ||1||
O lord of men, the pilgrim should then go to Rudrāvarta;
having bathed there, O King, a man is glorified in the heavenly world.
O best of men, one who bathes at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Sarasvatī obtains the merit of a horse sacrifice and goes to the heavenly world.
Having bathed there in the cavity of Karṇahrada and having worshipped the god Śaṅkara, one does not meet with an evil fate and goes to the heavenly world. ||4||
Thereafter, the pilgrim should proceed in due order to Kubjāmraka;
he obtains the merit of a thousand cows and goes to the heavenly world. ||5||
O lord of men, the pilgrim should go to Aruṇadhatīvaṭa;
having touched the waters at Sāmudraka and fasted for three nights, the man [attains merit].
One obtains the merit of giving a thousand cows and goes to the heavenly world;
from there, being composed and practicing celibacy, one should go to Brahmāvarta.
One obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice and goes to the heavenly world,
having gone to the source of the Yamunā and performed ablutions in its waters.
Having obtained the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice, one is glorified in the world of Brahmā.
One reaches the tirtha known as Darvīsaṃkramaṇa, which is renowned throughout the three worlds. ||9||
One obtains the merit of an Ashvamedha sacrifice and goes to the heavenly world;
having gone to the source of the Sindhu river, which is frequented by Siddhas and Gandharvas.
Having stayed there for five nights, one should give much gold;
then, having reached the goddess who is most difficult to attain, the man— ||11||
One obtains the merit of an Ashvamedha sacrifice and goes to the destination of Ushanas;
likewise, O Bharata, having reached Rishikulya and Vasishtha.
Transcending Vasiṣṭha, all twice-born castes are likewise [twice-born];
by bathing in the Ṛṣikulyā, a man attains the world of the sages. ||13||
O lord of men, if one should dwell there for a month subsisting on a diet of vegetables, having reached Bhṛgutuṅga, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice. ||14||
Having gone to Avīrapramokṣa, one is liberated from all sins;
likewise, by reaching the rare sacred ford (tīrtha) during the months of Kārttika and Māgha. ||15||
The performer of meritorious deeds obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma and Atirātra sacrifices;
thereafter, having reached the Sandhyā, he arrives at the unsurpassed Vidya-tīrtha.
One should perform ablutions; one shall become a master of all branches of knowledge. One should dwell for a night at Mahāśrama, which grants liberation from all sins. (17)
Eating only once a day, he dwelt in auspicious worlds; by fasting for six meals at a time, he lived for a month in the Great Abode.
Having crossed over himself, he enables ten ancestors and ten descendants to cross as well, having beheld this supreme merit of Maheśvara, which is saluted by the gods. (19)
Having accomplished all that was to be done, he should never grieve over death;
with his soul purified of all sins, he shall obtain the "Great Golden One" (Bahusuvarṇaka). 20.
Or, if one should go to Aśvatthikā, which was frequented by the Grandfather (Brahmā), one obtains the merit of a horse sacrifice and shall attain the supreme goal. ||21||
Then, having reached the Sundarika Tirtha frequented by the Siddhas, one becomes a possessor of beauty; this has been observed by the ancients.
Then, having gone to Brāhmaṇikā with a concentrated mind as a celibate student, he attains the world of Brahmā by means of a lotus-colored vehicle. ||23||
And from there, one should go to the holy Naimiṣa, frequented by the twice-born;
there Brahmā dwells eternally together with hosts of gods.
Half the sin of one who merely desires to go to Naimiṣa perishes;
but upon entering it, O King, he is liberated from all sins.
There, O wise one, intent upon that sacred site of Naimiṣa, one should dwell for a month;
for whatever sacred sites exist on earth, O Bhārata, they are all contained within Naimiṣa.
Having performed an ablution there, whether one's diet is restricted or unrestricted, that person obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya sacrifice. ||27||
O best of the Bharatas, he who, devoted to fasting, gives up his life at Naimiṣa purifies his lineage even unto the seventh generation.
O best of kings, even while residing in the heavenly world, the wise have said that Naimiṣa is eternally pure, auspicious, and meritorious.
Having reached Gaṅgodbheda and fasted for three nights,
a man obtains the Vājapeya sacrifice and shall forever become one with Brahman.
Having reached the Sarasvatī, one should offer libations to the ancestors and the gods;
he rejoices in the worlds of Sarasvatī—of this there is no doubt. (31)
Thereafter, O lord of men, the pilgrim should go to the Bāhudā;
by staying there for one night, he is glorified in the heavenly world.
A human being obtains the fruit of the Deva-sattra sacrifice;
thereafter, one should go to the holy Rajanī, which is frequented by Puṇyajanas. (33)
One who is devoted to the worship of the ancestors and the gods shall obtain the merit of the Vājapeya sacrifice;
having reached Vimalāśoka, he shines like the moon.
Having stayed there for one night, one is honored in the heavenly world;
from there, one should go to Gopratāra, the supreme sacred site on the banks of the Sarayū.
O King, by the power of that sacred ford, Rāma went to heaven along with his servants, army, and mounts, having abandoned his body there. 36.
O descendant of Bharata, O lord of men, by the grace of Rāma and through his resolve,
a man who bathes at that sacred ford, Gopratāra, [attains the highest goal].
O descendant of Kuru, having bathed at Rāmatīrtha on the Gomatī river, a man— his soul purified of all sins— is glorified in the heavenly world.
A man obtains the merit of a horse sacrifice and purifies his own lineage;
O best of the Bharatas, there is a sacred ford (tīrtha) there consisting of a hundred thousand [other sites]. (39)
Having performed the ritual sipping of water there, O bull of the Bharatas, one who is not restricted by fixed rules regarding food obtains the merit of giving a thousand cows. 40.
Then, O knower of dharma, a man should go to the unsurpassed Ūrdhvasthāna;
having bathed at Koṭitīrtha and having worshipped Guha, O King.
One obtains the merit of a thousand cows and becomes endowed with splendor;
then, having gone to Vārāṇasī and having worshipped the Bull-bannered Lord (Śiva), [one attains the same]. ||42||
Having bathed in the lake of the Kapilas, one obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya sacrifice;
O King of Kings, having reached that rare Tīrtha of Mārkaṇḍeya.
And at the world-renowned confluence of the Gomatī and the Gaṅgā, one obtains the merit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice and uplifts one's entire lineage. 44.
Thus ends the thirty-second chapter in the Svargakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa. ||32||
Chapter Thirty-three.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
You have related the greatness of Vārāṇasī in brief.
O Sage, speak in detail; that would please my mind.
Nārada said:
In this regard, I shall relate an ancient history concerning the virtues of Vārāṇasī,
by the mere hearing of which one is liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Formerly, on the peak of Mount Meru, the Goddess, seated upon her divine throne, questioned the Great God, Īśāna, the enemy of Tripura.
The Goddess said:
O Destroyer of the afflictions of those devoted to the Great God, the God of gods;
how does a person behold you, the Divine, in no long time? (4)
Sāṃkhya-yoga, as well as meditation (dhyāna), Vedic ritual action (karma-yoga),
and whatever other paths there are in this world, O Śaṅkara, are full of great exertion.
By this [means], the subtle Blessed One becomes visible to all embodied beings— both to yogis whose minds are undistracted and even to those engaged in ritual action.
This most secret knowledge is profound and practiced by Śakra and others;
for the benefit of all beings, speak it, [this] destroyer of the fire of desire. (7)
Īśvara said:

I shall declare to you, according to its true nature, that knowledge which is inexpressible, which is not understood by the ignorant, and which has been set aside by those lacking wisdom, as it was taught by the supreme seers.
My city of Vārāṇasī is the supreme and most secret field;
it carries all living beings across the ocean of saṃsāra. (9)
There, out of devotion to the Great Goddess, those high-souled ones dwell, established in my vow and observing supreme discipline. (10)
That which is the best of all holy fords, the best of all places, the best of all forms of knowledge—that supreme Avimukta is mine. 11.
There are sacred sites, holy fords, and shrines located in other places, as well as those situated in cremation grounds and those found in divine lands. (12)
This [world] is joined with the earth-world (bhūrloka), yet its abode is in the intermediate space (antarikṣa).
Those who are unliberated see it there; those who are liberated see it with the mind (cetas). 13.
This is the famous cremation ground known as Avimukta,
O beautiful one, where I, having become Time, withdraw this entire world.
O Goddess, this place is the most beloved of all secret places to me;
my devotees go there and enter into me alone. 15.
Whatever has been given, recited, offered in sacrifice, performed as ritual action, or practiced as austerity;
and whatever meditation, study, or knowledge has been acquired—all that shall become inexhaustible therein. (16)
Whatever sin has been accumulated previously over thousands of other births—all that goes to destruction for one who has entered Avimukta. (17)
Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and those of mixed castes; women, Mlecchas, and others who are born of impure wombs. ||18||
O fair-faced one, even insects, ants, and whatever other beasts and birds there may be,
they all meet their death in time within Avimukta.
O Goddess, in that city of Śiva, men are born with half-moons upon their crests, possessing three eyes, and having great bulls as their vehicles. (20)
No sinner who dies without being liberated goes to hell;
for all those favored by the Lord attain the supreme goal. 21.
Considering liberation to be extremely difficult to attain and saṃsāra to be most terrifying,
a man should dwell in Vārāṇasī, having bound his two feet with a stone.
O Supreme Goddess, even for one who has died in a place where [this knowledge] is difficult to obtain despite ascetic penance, the goal attained is that which liberates from saṃsāra. 23.
Through grace, my true nature is fully manifested to those who look toward me, O Lord of Mountains; yet those deluded by my māyā do not perceive it, for they have not attained spiritual maturity.
They dwell again and again in the midst of feces, urine, and semen;
yet that wise man who dwells [there] even while being struck by hundreds of obstacles [is truly steadfast].
They go to that supreme state, the abode of Śiva, which is the highest and where, having gone, one does not grieve; they reach that ultimate place, liberated from birth, death, and old age. ||26||
For those who desire liberation, this is the destination from which there is no returning to death;
having reached it, one has accomplished all that was to be done—thus do the wise consider it. (27)
Neither by gifts, nor by austerities, nor by knowledge of policy, nor even by learning is that supreme state attained; it is obtained only through liberation. (28)
There were those of various complexions and discolored, such as the despised Caṇḍālas and others,
their bodies filled with sins as well as with specific heinous crimes.
The wise know that the supreme medicine is liberation;
liberation is supreme knowledge, and liberation is the supreme state. (30)
Having performed the final initiatory rite (naiṣṭhikī-dīkṣā), those who dwell in Avimukta abide in the supreme reality, Avimukta, which is the supreme Śiva.
To them, at the end, I grant that supreme knowledge and the highest state;
[I grant] Prayāga, Naimiṣāraṇya, Śrīśaila, and Mahābala.
Kedāra, Bhadrakarṇa, Tugayā, Puṣkara, Kurukṣetra, Bhadrakoṭi, Narmadā, and Āmrātakeśvarī. (33)
Śālagrāma, Cakubjāmra, the unsurpassed Kokāmukha, Prabhāsa, Vijayeśāna, Gokarṇa, and Bhadrakarṇaka. ||34||
These places of merit, though renowned here throughout the three worlds, will not lead one to the supreme reality as effectively as dying in Vārāṇasī. (35)
In Vārāṇasī, the Gaṅgā, flowing through the three paths, especially destroys the sin committed over hundreds of previous births once she has entered [the city]. (36)
Wherever else śrāddha, charity, austerity, recitation, and vows are easily obtained, all of these are very difficult to find in Vārāṇasī. (37)
A man who dwells constantly in Vārāṇasī, subsisting only on air, should daily recite prayers, perform oblations, give gifts, and worship the immortals. (38)
Whether a man be sinful, whether he be deceitful, or even if he be unrighteous, upon reaching Vārāṇasī, he purifies his entire lineage. (39)
Those who worship and indeed praise Mahādeva in Vārāṇasī should be known as lords of the Gaṇas, liberated from all sins. ||40||
Except through yoga and knowledge, or through renunciation, or by some other means,
this supreme state is attained only after a thousand births.
Those devoted ones who indeed dwell in Vārāṇasī, the city of the Lord of the Gods, attain supreme liberation in that very same birth. 42.
Where there is yoga, there likewise is knowledge and liberation in a single birth;
having reached that Avimukta, one should desire no other grove of asceticism. 43.
Because it has not been abandoned by me, it is therefore known as Avimukta (the Unabandoned).
That alone is the secret of secrets; this is called the supreme knowledge. ||44||

O fair-browed one, that destination which is known for those who are devoted to knowledge or ignorance and who desire the highest bliss— that same destination belongs to the deceased who is liberated.
And those very things seen within the body of one who is not liberated are even more inauspicious than the cities and places such as Vārāṇasī. (46)
Where the Great God, the Lord himself, directly explains the Tāraka Brahman for the sake of liberation from this world, there indeed [is Avimukta]. 47.
That supreme reality which is known as Avimukta—one may attain it in a single birth by being in Vārāṇasī. 48.
In the middle of the eyebrows, in the middle of the navel, in the heart, and likewise in the head—just as the liberated [sun] is established in Āditya or in Vārāṇasī. ||49||
Likewise, in the middle of this Varaṇā lies the city of Vārāṇasī;
therein resides the reality that is eternally liberated. (50)
There has never been, nor will there ever be, a place superior to Vārāṇasī, where the god Nārāyaṇa, the Great God, the Lord of Heaven, resides. (51)
There, the gods, along with Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Uragas, and Rākṣasas,
constantly attend upon him, as does the Grandfather, the God of Gods.
O Goddess, even those who are great sinners, and among them those who have committed the most heinous crimes, attain the supreme goal upon reaching Vārāṇasī. (53)
Therefore, one who desires liberation should dwell with self-restraint until death in Vārāṇasī; having obtained knowledge from Mahādeva, he is liberated. ||54||
However, obstacles will arise for one whose mind is afflicted by evil;
therefore, one should not commit evil through body, mind, or speech. (55)
O lady of virtuous vows, this secret of the gods and the ancient seers—the knowledge that has its locus in Avimukta—is not known by anyone in its true essence. (56)
Nārada said:
While the deities, the sages, and the supreme beings were listening,
the God of gods recounted that which destroys all sins.
Just as Nārāyaṇa is the best among the gods, the Supreme Person; and just as Giriśa is the best among the lords, so this place is the most excellent among all stations. 58.
Those by whom the Great Rudra was propitiated in a previous birth know that supreme field, Avimukta, the abode of Śiva.
For those whose intellect has been impaired by the impurities produced in the Kali age,
it is impossible to know that abode of the Supreme Lord.
For those who always remember and speak of this city, their sins perish quickly both in this world and the next. (61)
Whatever sins those who have made their home here commit, may Lord Śiva, whose body is Time, destroy them all. (62)
One should come to this very place, frequented by those who long for liberation, so that there may be no further birth in the ocean of existence for those who have died here. (63)
Therefore, with every effort, a person should dwell in Vārāṇasī—whether they be a yogi or not a yogi, a sinner or one who has performed the most meritorious deeds. (64)
One's mind should not be turned away from the path to liberation by worldly talk, nor by the words of one's parents, nor even by the instructions of a teacher. (65)
Thus ends the thirty-third chapter in the Svargakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa. ||33||
(34) Chapter Thirty-Four.
Nārada said:
In this regard, there is this pure emblem named Oṃkāra, which is beautiful;
by the mere remembrance of it, one is liberated from all sins. (1)
This is the supreme knowledge, the highest of the five bases;
it is the liberation in Vārāṇasī, constantly practiced by the sages. (2)
There, the Blessed Lord Rudra, the Great God, who bestows liberation upon living beings, sports in person with his fivefold abode as his form. (3)
This Pāśupata knowledge is said to have five abodes;
it is this very stainless Liṅga, present as the syllable Om. ||4||
Śānti, Atiśānti, Vidyā, Aparā, and Avarā, as well as Pratiṣṭhā and Nivṛtti—this fivefold [set] is the divine Linga. ||5||
The Linga that is the common support for the five deities beginning with Brahmā, and which makes manifest the syllable Oṃ, is called Pañcāyatana. ||6||
One should remember the Lord as the immutable Liṅga of the five abodes;
the wise one enters that supreme light which is bliss itself within the body.
There, the celestial rishis, the ancient perfected ones, and likewise the brahmin rishis, having worshipped the Lord Īśāna as their object of adoration, attained the supreme state within.
O King of kings, on the meritorious banks of the Matsyodarī is a most auspicious and secret place, the supreme site of Oṃkāreśvara, which measures only the extent of a cow-hide.
The Kṛttivāseśvara Liṅga, the supreme Madhyameśvara,
likewise Viśveśvara, Oṃkāra, and Kaṃ Darpheśvara.
O Yudhiṣṭhira, no one here in Vārāṇasī knows these secret signs,
except by the grace of Śambhu.
O King, hear thus the majesty of Kṛttivāseśvara. In ancient times, at that very place, a Daitya, having become an elephant, [approached] the presence of Śiva.
I came to the place where the brahmins were constantly performing worship;
from their sacrificial marks, the three-eyed Great God manifested himself. (13)
For the sake of protecting his devotees, Mahādeva, who is affectionate toward his devotees, slew the Daitya in the form of an elephant with his trident and brought him down with contempt. 14.
Thereupon, Kṛttivāseśvara made his hide his garment;
O Yudhiṣṭhira, the two of them attained supreme perfection there. (15)
By means of that very body, they attained that supreme state;
they are celebrated as the Vidyās, the Vidyeśvaras, and the Rudras who are devoted to Śiva. ||16||
Knowing that the Kali Yuga is terrible and abounding in unrighteousness, people have remained constantly taking refuge in the Kṛttivāseśvara Liṅga. (17)
Those who bow to the one clad in an elephant hide have undoubtedly achieved their purpose;
for them, liberation will be attained either in this very life or within a thousand future births. 18.
Liberation is attained here at Krittivāsa within a single birth;
indeed, they call this place the abode of all the Siddhas. (19)
It was concealed by the God of gods, the Great God, the Blessed One; in every age, there are certain Brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Vedas. (20)
They wait upon the Great-Souled One, they mutter the Śatarudriya,
and they constantly praise the God Tryambaka, who is clothed in animal skins.
They meditate thus in their hearts upon Śiva, the motionless one who dwells within all.
The Siddhas indeed sing songs concerning Vārāṇasī, where the Brahmins dwell;
for them, liberation shall come through even one among them who has taken refuge in Kṛttivāsas. (22)

Having attained in this world birth in brahmin families—a boon desired by all beings and exceedingly difficult to obtain—these ascetics mutter the Rudra-mantra while absorbed in meditation, and they meditate upon Maheśvara within their hearts. (23)
Those sages dwelling in the midst of Vārāṇasī quickly propitiate the Lord, the Sovereign;
they sacrifice with sacrifices free from ulterior motives, they praise Rudra, and they bow down to the Source of Bliss.
Salutations to Bhava, the abode of the yoga of immortality; I take refuge in Sthāṇu, the ancient Giriśa.
I remember Rudra seated within the heart; I know the Great God of manifold forms. 25.
Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter in the Svargakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa. ||34||
(35) Chapter Thirty-Five.
Nārada said:
Now, O King, there is another supreme Liṅga there called Kapardīśvara;
having bathed there according to the prescribed rite, one should offer libations to the ancestors.
One is liberated from all sins and attains both liberation and worldly enjoyment. Beyond that stands another sacred site named Piśācamocana. ||2||
There, the Lord made of jewels, the bestower of liberation and the destroyer of all defects, was present;
then a certain Daitya, assuming a terrible form like a tiger, approached him.
In order to devour a certain doe, she went to the supreme Kapardīśvara;
there, with a terrified heart, she performed circumambulation after circumambulation. ||4||
Running in great agitation, she fell into the power of a tiger;
the exceedingly powerful tiger tore her apart with his sharp claws. ||5||
Having seen the lords of sages, she went to another secluded place; and that young girl, a doe, died right there in front of Kapardīśa immediately upon her arrival.
Possessing the brilliance of the sun in the sky with a great, most invisible flame,
she has three eyes, a blue throat, and hair adorned with the moon.
Surrounded by such men mounted upon bulls,
the sky-dwellers then released a rain of flowers simultaneously with that.
Having herself become Gaṇeśvarī, she was not seen there at that moment;
then, having witnessed that most wonderful marvel, the gods and others offered praise. ||9||
That supreme Liṅga of Maheśa, Kapardīśvara—the mere remembrance of which causes one to be swiftly liberated from the entire multitude of sins. ||10||
All defects such as lust, anger, and the like, as well as all obstacles for the residents of Vārāṇasī, perish through the worship of Kapardīśvara. (11)
Therefore, the supreme Kapardīśvara should always be beheld;
he should be worshipped with diligence and praised with Vedic hymns. 12.
And for those yogis who meditate here with a restrained mind and a peaceful heart, the perfection of yoga will surely arise within six months; of this there is no doubt.
By worshipping him, sins such as the killing of a Brahmin are destroyed;
for through bathing in the Piśācamocana pool, one attains complete peace.
In that sacred field, there was formerly a brahmin ascetic of strict vows, renowned as Śaṅkukarṇa, who worshipped Śaṅkara. ||15||
He incessantly chanted the Praṇava, which is Rudra and the very form of Brahman, with flowers, incense, and other offerings, as well as with hymns, prostrations, and circumambulations. ||16||
Having performed the *iṣṭikī* initiation, he should practice yoga there;
however, he once saw a deceased person who had arrived, overcome by hunger.
Seeing that body bound with skin and bone, sighing again and again, that best of sages was filled with supreme compassion. (18)
"From what country have you come to take refuge in this land?
To him, the Piśāca, tormented by hunger, spoke these words: (19)
In a previous birth, I was a Brahmin endowed with wealth and grain;
possessed of sons, grandsons, and others, I was intent on maintaining my family. (20)
Neither were the great gods, nor cows, nor guests ever worshipped by him;
nor was any merit ever performed, whether small or even great. (21)
Once, the Blessed Lord, the God whose vehicle is the bull, the Lord of the Universe, was seen, touched, and saluted by me in Vārāṇasī. (22)
Then, after a short time, I met my death;
yet, O Sage, that most terrible abode of Yama was not seen by me.
"O Lord, we who are now overcome by thirst do not know what is beneficial or harmful;
if you see any means whatsoever to deliver us from this, [please tell us]. (24)
"Perform this; salutations to you, for I have come to you for refuge.
Thus addressed, Śaṅkukarṇa then spoke these words to the piśāca: ||25||
There is no one else in this world who has performed such supreme merit as you, by whom the Blessed Lord Śiva, the Sovereign of the Universe, was previously beheld. (26)
Having been touched by this and having experienced even more suffering, who else on earth is like you?
By the ripening of that karma, I have come to this place. (27)
"Perform your bath quickly in this pool with a concentrated mind, by which you shall swiftly abandon this contemptible womb. (28)

Having been thus addressed by the compassionate sage Piśāca, he called to mind the three-eyed Lord of the gods, Kapardīśvara, the Sovereign; and having fixed his mind upon Him, he entered into meditative absorption.
Then, having descended into the presence of the Sage, Māra appeared, adorned with divine ornaments,
resembling the sun in his celestial chariot, with a beautiful crown marked by the crescent moon.

This God, the Lord of all gods, shines forth accompanied by the Rudras dwelling in heaven, brought together with the Yogins who are immeasurable as mountains, along with the Vālakhilyas and others, just as the sun rises accompanied by its rays.
The hosts of gods, including the Siddhas, offer praise; the delightful celestial Apsarases dance;
and the Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, Kinnaras, and others release a rain mixed with flowers and water. (32)
Then, being praised by the hosts of lords of sages and having attained enlightenment through the grace of the Blessed One,
he entered this foremost maṇḍala consisting of the three Vedas, wherein Rudra shines forth.
Seeing Maheśa liberated along with the piśāca and bhūta, the sage was delighted in his mind; reflecting upon Rudra as the one Seer and the Fire, he bowed and praised that Kapardin.
Śaṅkukarṇa said:
I go for refuge to You, the one with matted hair, who is beyond the beyond, the sole protector, the ancient Puruṣa;
the Lord of Yoga, the fulfiller of desires, the Sun, the Fire, mounted upon Kapila.
I go for refuge to you, Rudra, who reside in the heart as the golden yogi, the primordial essence of Brahman, dwelling in the heavens.
The great sage, consisting of Brahman, the pure one. ||36||

I bow to that auspicious one, who possesses a thousand feet, eyes, and heads, who has a thousand forms and stands beyond darkness; to him, the shore of Brahman, the Lord of Hiraṇyagarbha, the three-eyed Śambhu. (37)
I perpetually bow to and take refuge in that Blessed Lord, the shore of Brahman, the Sovereign, from whom the birth of the world proceeds and by whom all this is pervaded with auspiciousness. ||38||

I shall bow to you, the signless one whose form is devoid of light, the self-sovereign Lord, the singular Master of consciousness, the Supreme Lord who is the further shore of Brahman; for there exists nothing other than you. (39)

I bow eternally to that God, the further shore of Brahman and the supreme essential nature, whom yogis—having abandoned yoga with seed and attained samādhi—behold as having become one with the Supreme Self. 40.

I perpetually bow to that shore of Brahman, whose nature does not abide within the range of perception and wherein there is no conceptual construction of names or other distinctions; I take refuge in you, the Self-existent One. 41.

I perpetually bow to You, the further shore of Brahman, whom those devoted to the declarations of the Vedas perceive as the one, undivided, and non-dual consciousness of Brahman within the bodiless state, yet who appear to them as manifold according to their own nature. 42.
Since the Pradhāna, the ancient Puruṣa, and the Devas bow down to that splendor which you, the Great Time, sustain as your own essential nature—residing within the light—I bow to that. 43.
I go for refuge eternally to Guheśa; I take shelter of Sthāṇu, the ancient Giriśa.
I take refuge in Śiva, Hari, the moon-crested one; I go for refuge to you, the wielder of the Pināka bow. ||44||
Having thus praised the Lord Kapardin for his auspiciousness,
Śaṅkukarṇa fell upon the ground like a staff, uttering the supreme Praṇava.
At that very moment, a supreme linga of the nature of Śiva appeared—consisting of pure knowledge, immeasurable, and resembling a fire with ten million flames. 46.
Then Śaṃkukarṇa, whose soul was liberated, merged into that stainless Self which pervades all;
he vanished into the pure Liṅga, and it was like a marvel. ||47||
This secret, this majesty of the one with matted hair (Kapardin), has been declared to you;
no one knows it, for even the learned man is deluded therein by darkness. 48.
Whoever should constantly hear this narrative that destroys sin, having abandoned sin and purified in soul, shall attain proximity to Rudra. ||49||
One who is pure should constantly recite this great hymn, the *Brahmapāra*;
at dawn and at midday, he shall attain the supreme yoga. (50)
Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter, titled "The Greatness of Vārāṇasī," in the Svargakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
(36) Chapter Thirty-Six.
Nārada said:
In Vārāṇasī, in the midst of the great kings, is Madhyameśa, the supreme among the supreme;
in that place dwells Mahādeva, the Great Lord, together with the Goddess. ||1||
The Blessed One, surrounded by the Rudras, rejoices there eternally;
there, in the beginning, was Hṛṣīkeśa, the soul of the universe, the son of Devakī.
For one full year, Kṛṣṇa remained constantly accompanied by the Pāśupatas;
his entire body was smeared with ashes, and he was devoted to the study of the Rudrādhyāya.
Worshiping Lord Śambhu and having performed the Pāśupata vow,
Hari had many disciples who were devoted to the practice of celibacy.
Having received that knowledge from his mouth and having beheld Maheśvara—
the Great God Nīlalohita— who was visibly present before them— 5.
The Blessed One, the giver of boons, granted this supreme boon to Kṛṣṇa:
"Those who are my devotees and worship Govinda according to the prescribed rites," (6)
Then, that divine knowledge consisting of the universe will arise within them;
they shall be saluted, worshipped, and meditated upon by people who have transcended the world.
There is no doubt that those twice-born ones who,
having bathed here, behold the Lord of Gods, the divine wielder of the Pināka bow, shall [attain their goal] through my grace.
The sin of killing a Brahmin and other such evils of theirs is quickly destroyed;
even those mortals who are devoted to sinful deeds will renounce their lives [there]. (9)
They go to that supreme state; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
Blessed indeed are those who have offered water-oblations to the Ḍākinīs. (10)
Having worshipped the Great God, the Lord Madhyameśvara,
[one should perform] here knowledge, charity, austerity, the ancestral śrāddha rite, and the offering of funeral cakes.
An action performed even once purifies the family up to the seventh generation;
likewise for one who touches the waters at Sannihatī when the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu.
Whatever fruit a mortal obtains there, ten times that is obtained here;
thus has the greatness of Mahārāja at Madhyameśvara been described.
Whoever hears this with supreme devotion attains the highest state. ||13||
Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, titled "The Greatness of Vārāṇasī," in the Svargakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
(37) The Thirty-Seventh Chapter.
Nārada said:
And there are other purifying great royal tirthas situated here in Varanasi; listen to them, O Yudhisthira.
Prayāga is a sacred site superior [to others], the supreme and most auspicious Prayāga;
likewise, there is the Viśvarūpa Tīrtha and the unsurpassed Tāla Tīrtha. ||2||
The great pilgrimage site called Ākāśa, the supreme pilgrimage site of Arṣabha, the great pilgrimage site Sunīla, and the unsurpassed Gaurī-tīrtha. ||3||
Likewise, there is the Prājāpatya tīrtha and likewise Svargadvāra;
that which is called Jambukeśvara is the supreme tīrtha known as Dharmākhya. ||4||
Gayātīrtha is a supreme sacred site, as is the great river Tīrtha;
Nārāyaṇatīrtha is a supreme sacred site, and Vāyutīrtha is unsurpassed. ||5||
The supreme secret Jñānatīrtha, the most excellent Vārāha-tīrtha, the meritorious Yamatīrtha, and the auspicious Saṃmūrtika-tīrtha. ||6||
The Agnitīrtha, the supreme Kalaseśvara of the Great King, as well as the Nāgatīrtha, the Somatīrtha, and likewise the Sūryatīrtha. ||7||
The great secret known as Parvata, the unsurpassed Maṇikarṇika, the excellent tīrtha Ghaṭotkaca, and the venerable Śrītīrtha Capitāmaha. ||8||
The Gaṅgātīrtha, the Deveśa, the supreme Tīrtha of Yayāti, the Kāpila, the Someśa, and the unsurpassed Brahmatīrtha. (9)
There, just as Brahmā had gone to establish the ancient Liṅga,
Viṣṇu then installed the Lord of Taila.
Having bathed there and returned, Brahmā said to that Hari:
"Why have you installed this linga which was brought by me? (11)
Viṣṇu said to him: "O Rudra, my devotion to you is even firmer than yours;
therefore, the installed Liṅga shall be known by your name. (12)
Likewise, there is the Bhūteśvara Tīrtha, the Tīrtha from which Dharma originated, the most auspicious Gandharva Tīrtha, and the excellent Vāhneya Tīrtha. (13)
Daurvāsika, Vyomatīrtha, Candratīrtha, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the Cintā-tīrtha, Gadeśvara-tīrtha, and the meritorious Vidyādhareśvara. ||14||
The sacred ford of Kedāra known as Ugra, Kālañjara which is unsurpassed, Sārasvata, Prabhāsa, and the auspicious Rudrakoṭi-hrada. ||15||
The great holy site named Kokila, the holy site of Mahālaya, Hiraṇyagarbha, and the unsurpassed holy site of Goprekṣa. ||16||
Upaśānta and Śiva, as well as the unsurpassed Vyāghreśvara;
Trilocana, the great tīrtha, and Lokārka, which is called Uttarā. ||17||
The sacred ford Kapālamocana destroys the sin of killing a Brahmin;
Śukreśvara is of great merit, as is the supreme Ānandapura. ||18||
Such holy places as these are indeed situated in Vārāṇasī;
it is not possible to describe them in detail even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, titled "The Greatness of Vārāṇasī," in the Svargakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
The thirty-eighth chapter.
Nārada said:
O Lord, [tell me] the majesty of Vārāṇasī and the sacred fords (tīrthas) within it.
These sacred fords have been described in brief; now listen to others. ||1||
Then, having reached Gayā while remaining celibate and composed,
one obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice simply by going there, O Bhārata.
O Lord, where the banyan tree named Akṣayya-vaṭa is renowned throughout the three worlds, there the offering made to the ancestors becomes inexhaustible. ||3||
Having touched the waters of a great river, one should offer libations to the ancestors and the deities;
thus one shall attain imperishable worlds and indeed uplift one's entire lineage. ||4||
Then, having crossed the Brahmasaras lake frequented by the forest of Brahmā,
one attains Puṇḍarīka, as the night reaches its dawn.
There, the Sarasī Brahmin erected an excellent sacrificial post (yūpa).
By circumambulating that post, one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice. ||6||
From there, O king of kings, one should go to Dhenuka, which is world-renowned;
having stayed for one night, O King, one should offer a cow made of sesame seeds.
One whose self is purified of all sins shall certainly go to the world of the Moon;
O Great King, the sign of this remains there even today, without a doubt. (8)
A tawny cow, accompanied by her calf, roams about on the mountain;
O Bhārata, even today her footprints can still be seen.
O best of kings, O descendant of Bharata, by touching those waters at the sites of the lords of kings, whatever inauspicious sin there may be, that is utterly destroyed.
Thereafter, one should go to Gṛdhravaṭa, the abode of the trident-bearing God;
having approached the Bull-bannered Lord there, one should bathe with sacred ash.
If a Brāhmaṇa has performed the twelve-year vow, then for the other castes, all sin is destroyed. ||12||
From there, O bull of the Bharatas, one should go today to that mountain resounding with songs; there, the footprint of Savitṛ is seen.
There, a Brāhmaṇa of firm vows should perform the twilight worship;
by performing it thus, the twilight worship becomes equivalent to twelve years.
And there, O bull of the Bharatas, is the place renowned as Yonidvāra;
by approaching that, a man is said to be liberated from the distress of rebirth.
O King, whatever man should dwell at Gayā during both the bright and dark fortnights, he purifies his lineage up to the seventh generation; there is no doubt in this matter.
Many sons are to be desired, for even if one among them goes to Gayā, or performs the Aśvamedha sacrifice, or releases a dark-colored bull. (17)
Thereafter, O King, the pilgrim should go to Phalgu, O lord of men;
he obtains the merit of a horse sacrifice and attains supreme perfection. ||18||
From there, O king of kings, one should proceed with a concentrated mind to Dharmapṛṣṭha,
where Dharma, O great king Yudhiṣṭhira, eternally resides.
Having approached Dharma there, one obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice;
from there, O king of kings, one should go to the supreme tirtha of Brahmā.
There, one who is firm in his vows should approach and worship Brahmā;
O Bhārata, he obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.
From there, O lord of men, one who frequents sacred fords should go to Rājagṛha;
having performed ablutions there, he rejoices like Kakṣīvān.
There, a pure man should daily offer oblations to the Yakṣiṇī before the fire;
by the grace of the Yakṣiṇī, he is liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin.
From there, one should go to Maṇināga; such a person obtains the merit of giving a thousand cows.
That man who eats the daily meal at Maṇināga [attains this fruit]. ||24||
O King, the poison of a venomous serpent does not spread within one who has been bitten;
by staying there for a single night, he is liberated from all sins. (25)
From there, O King, one should go to the forest of the Brahman-sage Gautama;
having bathed in the lake of Ahalyā, one shall attain the supreme goal.
O King, having approached Śrī, one obtains supreme prosperity;
there, O knower of dharma, is a well renowned throughout the three worlds.
One should perform an ablution there; one would thereby obtain the merit of a horse sacrifice.
There is also the well of the royal sage Janaka, which is honored by the thirty gods.
Having performed an ablution there, one shall attain the world of Viṣṇu;
from there, one should go to Avināśana, which grants liberation from all sins. ||29||
One obtains the merit of a horse sacrifice (vājimedha) and goes to the world of Soma, having reached the Gaṇḍakī river, which arises from the waters of all sacred fords (tīrthas). ||30||
He obtains the Vājapeya sacrifice and goes to the world of the Sun;
then, O knower of dharma, having entered the ascetic grove of Dhruva, [he dwells there]. 31.
O highly fortunate one, there is no doubt that one rejoices among the Guhyakas here by reaching the river Karmadā, which is frequented by the Siddhas. (32)
One obtains the Puṇḍarīka [fruit] and goes to the world of Soma;
then, having reached the river Viśālā, which is renowned throughout the three worlds. ||33||
One obtains the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice and goes to the heavenly world;
furthermore, O lord of men, by reaching this stream of Maheśvara, one attains these rewards.
A pure man, having reached the lotus-pool of the gods, obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice and uplifts his entire lineage. (35)
He does not fall into an evil rebirth and attains the merit of the Vājapeya sacrifice;
then, being self-controlled and observant of celibacy, he shall go to the station of Maheśa.
Having bathed at Māheśvara-pada, one obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice;
there, O bull of the Bharatas, ten million sacred fords (tīrthas) are renowned. (37)
O King of kings, while she was being carried away by a wicked-souled asura in the form of a tortoise,
O King, she was recovered by the all-powerful Viṣṇu.
O lord of men, one should perform an ablution there at Koṭitīrtha;
one obtains the merit of the Puṇḍarīka sacrifice and goes to the world of Viṣṇu. ||39||
From there, O best of men, one should go to the abode of Nārāyaṇa,
where Hari always dwells in constant presence, O Bhārata.
There, the gods beginning with Brahmā, the sages whose wealth is austerity,
the Ādityas, Vasus, and Rudras, worship Janārdana.
The Śālagrāma is renowned as the abode of Viṣṇu, whose deeds are marvelous;
it is the place where one may approach Acyuta Viṣṇu, the Lord of the three worlds and the bestower of boons.
One obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice and goes to the world of Viṣṇu;
there, O knower of dharma, is a well that liberates one from all sins.
The four oceans are always present there within the well; having sipped water there, O lord of kings, one shall not fall into a miserable state. 44.
Having approached the great god Viṣṇu, the giver of boons and the imperishable one, O Yudhiṣṭhira, he shines like the moon freed from its debts. 45.
One who remembers their past births, having touched [the water] and become pure with a restrained mind, attains the memory of past lives by bathing there; of this there is no doubt. (46)
Having gone to Vaṭeśvarapura and having worshipped Keśava, people obtain their desired worlds through fasting; of this there is no doubt. (47)
Then, having gone to Vāmana, which destroys all sins, and having paid homage to the divine Hari, one shall not meet with an evil fate. ||48||
Having gone to Bharata’s hermitage, which liberates one from all sins, one should there resort to the Kauśikī river, which destroys even the most heinous crimes. 49.
A human being obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya sacrifice;
from there, one who knows dharma should go to the supreme Caṃpakāraṇya. (50)
Having stayed there for one night, one obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows;
then, having reached the most highly esteemed pilgrimage site of Govinda, [one obtains further merit]. (51)
Having fasted for one night, one obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice;
there, having beheld Viśveśvara together with the Goddess of great splendor. (52)
O bull among the Bharatas, one shall attain the worlds of Mitra and Varuṇa;
having fasted there for three nights, one obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. (53)
Having reached Kanyāvasatha, self-restrained and restricted in his diet, O bull of the Bharatas, he attains the worlds of Manu Prajāpati. 54.
O Bhārata, those who bestow even a small gift upon a maiden—
sages of strict vows declare that such a gift is inexhaustible.
Having reached Niṣṭhāvāsa, which is renowned throughout the three worlds, one obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice and goes to the world of Viṣṇu. ||56||
But those men who bestow gifts with a sense of completion,
O tiger among men, go to the healthy world of Brahmā.
There lies the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha, renowned throughout the three worlds;
performing an ablution there, one obtains the merit of the Vājapeya sacrifice. (58)
Having reached Devakūṭa, which is frequented by hosts of gods and sages, one obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice and uplifts one's entire lineage. (59)
From there, O king of kings, one should go to the lake of the sage Kauśika;
it was there that Viśvāmitra, the son of Kuśika, attained supreme perfection.
O bull of the Bharata race, whatever merit is obtained from an Ashvamedha sacrifice, that wise man attains by staying for one month at the Kauśikī.
Whoever should dwell at that great lake, the best of all sacred fords (tīrtha), shall not fall into an evil state; one should know that he will obtain much gold.
Having approached the Kumāra who dwells in the Vīra hermitage, one obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice and goes to the world of Śakra. ||63||
O best of the Kurus, having reached the well known as Dinyā, which is frequented by the gods, one obtains that merit which belongs to a human sacrifice (naramedha).
Having bathed at the confluence of the Kālikā with the Kauśikī and the Aruṇā,
a wise man who fasts for three nights is liberated from all sins.
Having reached the Urvaśī-tīrtha and likewise the Soma-āśrama by the ocean,
and having bathed at the Kuṃbhakarṇa-āśrama, a man is honored on earth.
Likewise, having bathed at Kokāmukha while remaining celibate and composed, one attains the memory of past births; this has been witnessed by the ancients.
Having reached the river even once, the twice-born becomes one who has accomplished his purpose;
with his soul purified of all sins, he goes to the heavenly world. ||68||
Having reached Ṛṣabhadvīpa and having served the destroyer of Krauñca,
and having sipped water at the Sarasvatī, one shines resplendent seated in a celestial chariot.
At Audyānaka, the great royal tīrtha frequented by sages, one should perform an ablution; there, one is liberated from all sins. (70)
Having reached the holy Brahmatīrtha, which is frequented by Brahmanical sages, a man obtains the merit of the Vājapeya sacrifice; of this there is no doubt.
Then, having reached the confluence of the Pañcanada and performed the water-libation in the Bhāgīrathī, one obtains the merit of donating a thousand cows upon reaching Daṇḍārpaṇa. ||72||
One should go from there to Lāviḍhikā, a holy place frequented by the meritorious;
one obtains the merit of a Vājapeya sacrifice and is honored while seated in a celestial chariot.
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Greatness of Gayā and Other Holy Places," in the Svargakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
The thirty-ninth chapter.
Nārada said: Then, having reached the excellent sacred ford (tīrtha) known as Savidyā at the time of twilight (saṃdhyā),...
A wise man who touches [this water] shall become learned; there is no doubt in this matter. ||1||
In ancient times, by the grace of Rāma, that king of tīrthas was made [sacred]; having reached that Lauhitya, one should know it as Bahusuvarṇaka. ||2||
Having reached the Karatoyā and fasted there for three nights, a man obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice and goes to the world of Śakra. ||3||
O king of kings, at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean,
the wise declare that the merit is ten times that of an Aśvamedha sacrifice.
O descendant of Bharata, O King, he who reaches the further island of the Gaṅgā and bathes there, having fasted for three nights, shall obtain all his desires. (5)
Then, having gone to the river Vaitaraṇī which liberates one from sin,
and having reached the sacred ford Viraja, he shines like the moon.
Having purified his lineage through its power, he casts off all evil;
having obtained the fruit of a thousand cows, that man sanctifies his own family. ||7||
Dwelling at the confluence of the Śoṇa and the Jyotirathyā, pure and having offered libations to the ancestors and the gods, one obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. ||8||
O bull among the Kurus, by touching the Vaṃśagulma at the source of the Śoṇa and the Narmadā,
one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
O lord of men, having reached the Ṛṣabha Tīrtha in Kośalā,
a man who fasts for three nights obtains the merit of a horse sacrifice.
Having reached Kālatīrtha in Kośalā, one should perform ablutions;
there he obtains the merit of eleven bulls—of this there is no doubt. ||11||
Having sipped water at Puṣpavatī and fasted for three nights, a man obtains the merit of giving a thousand cows and uplifts his entire lineage. ||12||
Then, having bathed at the Badarīka-tīrtha with a restrained mind, one attains long life and goes to the heavenly world. ||13||
Then, having reached Mahendra, which was frequented by the son of Jamadagni,
a man who bathes at Rāmatīrtha shall obtain the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
O bull among the Bharatas, it is held that one should go to Kedāra;
having bathed there, a man shall obtain the fruit of ten thousand horse-sacrifices. 15.
Having reached Śrīparvata, one should perform ablutions on the riverbank;
one obtains the merit of a horse sacrifice and attains supreme perfection. ||16||
On Śrīparvata, the Great God of supreme luster dwelt together with the Goddess, exceedingly pleased, as did Brahmā surrounded by the thirty gods. ||17||
Having bathed there at Devahrada, pure and with a restrained mind, one obtains the merit of an Ashvamedha sacrifice and attains supreme perfection. ||18||
Having gone to Mount Ṛṣabha, which is worshipped by the gods,
one obtains the merit of the Vājapeya sacrifice and rejoices in the vault of heaven.
From there, one should go to the Kāverī, which is surrounded by throngs of celestial nymphs;
having bathed there, a person obtains the fruit of ten thousand sacrifices. 20.
There, at the sacred ford of the ocean, one should perform ablutions at Kanyātīrtha;
having performed ablutions there, O Indra among kings, one is liberated from all sins.
Then, O king of kings, having reached Gokarṇa, renowned throughout the three worlds and situated in the midst of the ocean, which is honored by all the worlds. ||22||
Wherein dwell the gods beginning with Brahmā, as well as sages whose wealth is their asceticism,
along with spirits, yakṣas, piśācas, kinnaras, and great serpents.
Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, humans, as well as Pannagas,
rivers, oceans, and mountains worship the Lord of Umā.
Having worshipped Īśāna there, a man who has fasted for three nights obtains the merit of ten horse-sacrifices and attains the status of a leader of Gaṇas. ||25||
Having fasted for twelve nights, a man becomes one who has accomplished his purpose;
for in that very place is the station of Gāyatrī, renowned throughout the three worlds. (26)
Having stayed there for three nights, one obtains the fruit of a thousand cows;
and the proof of this, O lord of men, is directly perceptible to the Brahmins.
O King, for that twice-born man who recites the Gāyatrī while having sexual intercourse with his wife,
his speech becomes like that of a song or a melody.
The *sāvitrī* of one who is not a Brahmin perishes as he recites it;
yet for that eminent sage, even though he had reached a difficult-to-attain well, it returned to him. 29.
He becomes a sharer in beauty and is born fortunate;
thereafter, having reached the Veṇā river, he should offer libations to the ancestors and the gods. ||30||
A person obtains a celestial chariot adorned with peacocks and swans;
thereafter, having reached the Godāvarī, which is constantly frequented by the Siddhas. ||31||
One attains the Gavāmaya sacrifice and goes to the world of Vāyu;
having bathed at the confluence of the Veṇā, one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice. ||32||
Having bathed at Varadāsaṅgama, one obtains the merit of giving a thousand cows;
having reached Brahmasthūṇā, a man who fasts for three nights [obtains the same]. ||33||
Having reached Kubjāvana with a concentrated mind and observing celibacy, one obtains the merit of a thousand cows and goes to the heavenly world. (34)
Having fasted for three nights and bathed at Devahrada, which is formed from the waters of the Kṛṣṇaveṇā, one obtains the merit of giving a thousand cows.
And likewise, O King, at the Jyotirmātra lake and at Kanyāśrama,
where the king of the gods, having performed a hundred sacrifices, ascended to heaven.
By merely going there, one obtains the merit of a hundred Agniṣṭoma sacrifices;
having bathed in all the lakes of the gods, one gains the fruit of giving a thousand cows. ||37||
By bathing at Jātimātrahrada, a man shall become one who remembers his past births;
and by going to Śarabhaṅgāśrama and that of the high-souled Śuka, [he attains the same]. (38)
One devoted to the worship of the ancestors and the gods shall obtain the fruit of a thousand cows;
having reached the Daṇḍaka forest, O great king, one should perform ablutions. (39)
Having gone to Śarabhaṅga’s hermitage and that of the high-souled Aṣṭāvakra, a man does not meet with an evil fate; he purifies his own lineage. ||40||
Thence one should go to Sūryāraka, frequented by Jamadagni;
having bathed at Rāmatīrtha, a man shall obtain much gold.
Having bathed at Saptagodāvarī, being self-restrained and restricted in diet, one obtains great merit and goes to the world of the gods. ||42||
Then, one who is self-restrained and moderate in eating should proceed to Devapatha;
that man obtains the merit which belongs to the Devasatra sacrifice.
In ancient times, Sārasvata, having become a celibate student with his senses subdued, reached the forest of Tuṅga and there taught the Vedas to the sages.
There, O Bhārata, the son of the sage Āṅgirasa sat upon the upper garments of the great ṛṣis while the lost Vedas were being recited.
By the syllable *Oṃ*, when properly and correctly uttered according to the rules,
whatever was previously practiced by one returns to that person.
The sages and the gods were there—Varuṇa, Agni, Prajāpati, the god Hari Nārāyaṇa, and likewise Mahādeva. ||47||
And the blessed Grandfather, of great splendor, together with the gods, appointed the highly effulgent Bhṛgu for the purpose of performing the sacrifice. 48.
Then the Blessed One, together with the sages,
duly performed the re-establishment of the sacred fires for everyone through a rite witnessed by the gods.
Having been gratified there according to the prescribed rite with their portions of clarified butter, the gods departed for the three worlds and the sages likewise went as they pleased. (50)
O best of kings, for one who has entered that forest, whether a woman or a man, sin is destroyed instantly. (51)
There, O King, the wise man should dwell for a month, restrained and with a regulated diet;
he shall go to the world of Brahmā and further purify his lineage.
Having reached Medhāvana, one should offer libations to the ancestors and the gods;
one obtains the merit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice and attains memory and intelligence. ||53||
Having spent his time there until old age, one obtains the fruit of a thousand cows;
O King, one should perfect oneself by spending one's life there on that mountain.
That man shall be honored in the heavenly world; of this there is no doubt.
Thereafter, O lord of the people, [he shall go] to Citrakūṭa, the best of mountains, the king of peaks.
Having reached me, the ḍākinī, the river that liberates from sin,
one who performs the consecration here and is devoted to the worship of the ancestors and the gods— ||56||
One obtains the merit of an Ashvamedha sacrifice and shall go to the supreme goal;
from there, O king of kings, one should proceed to the unsurpassed Guhasthāna.
O King, wherever the god Mahāsena is eternally present, there a man becomes a supreme person; merely by going there, he attains success. 58.
Having bathed at Koṭitīrtha, a man obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows;
then, having performed a circumambulation, he should proceed to the abode of Yaśas.
Having approached the great god, he shines like the moon;
there, O bull of the Bharatas, is the famous great king of wells. 60.
O Yudhiṣṭhira, having touched the water and performed a circumambulation there, where the four oceans dwell, O lord of kings; ||61||
A man of self-restraint, being purified, shall go to the supreme goal;
from there, O best of the Kurus, he should go to the great Śṛṅgaverapura.
Where in former times the highly wise Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, crossed over;
there, having bathed in the Gaṅgā, one who is celibate and has conquered his senses [is purified]. 63.
His sins are shaken off and he obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice;
thereafter, he should go to that place, the abode of the wise deity, Javaṭa.
Having approached the Great God and worshipped him, O King, and having performed a circumambulation, one shall attain the status of a Gaṇapati. ||65||
From there, O king of kings, one should go to Prayāga, praised by the sages,
where Brahmā and the other gods, along with the quarters and the lords of the directions, reside.
The world-protectors, the Siddhas, and the devoted ancestors, as well as the great seers headed by Sanatkumāra, [were present]. ||67||
Likewise, the Nāgas and Suparṇas, the Siddhas who bear the seed, as well as the rivers, the oceans, and the Gandharvas and Apsarases. ||68||
And the blessed Hari sits there, preceded by Prajāpati;
there are three sacrificial pits there, and between them flows the Jāhnavī.
Passing beyond Prayāga, that daughter of the Sun, honored by all sacred fords, is renowned throughout the three worlds. (70)
Where the world-creating Yamunā meets with the Gaṅgā, the region between the Gaṅgā and Yamunā is known as the hips of the Earth. (71)
The sages know Prayāga to be the end of the hips, the lap;
and both Supratiṣṭhāna and the two [sages] Kambala and Aśvatara are Prayāga. (72)
The sacred ford Bhogavatī is said to be the altar of Prajāpati;
there, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the Vedas and the sacrifices exist in embodied form.
O King, the great sages and the gods worshipped Prajāpati with sacrifices; likewise, they worshipped the wielders of the discus [Viṣṇu]. 74.
Therefore, O Bhārata, there is nothing more meritorious in the three worlds than Prayāga; it is superior in power to all other tīrthas, O Lord. (75)
By hearing of that sacred ford, by the mere chanting of its name,
or even by bowing one's head to it, one is liberated from all sins.
Whoever, firm in their vows, should perform an ablution there at the confluence, obtains the very great merit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices. (77)
For this is indeed the sacrificial ground even for the gods;
O Bhārata, whatever is given there, however small, becomes great. (78)
O dear one, your mind should not be diverted from the thought of dying at Prayāga, neither by the words of the gods nor even by the words of the world. (79)
Ten thousand holy fords (tīrtha) and sixty crores of others—the presence of which is proclaimed right here, O descendant of Kuru. (80)
Whatever merit lies in the four Vedas and whatever merit lies in those who speak the truth,
one who has bathed at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā obtains all that.
Beyond that is the supreme holy site of Vāsuki, known as Bhogavatī;
he who performs an ablution there shall obtain the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice. ||82||
There, O descendant of Kuru, is the world-renowned ford known as Saprapatana,
as well as Daśāśvamedhika on the Gaṅgā.
The Gaṅgā is equal to Kurukṣetra wherever she is bathed in;
however, there is a special distinction at Vikaṇakhala, which is a supreme and great Prayāga.
If one has committed a hundred improper deeds but has not performed service to the Gaṅgā,
all of that is consumed by the water of the Gaṅgā, just as fire consumes wealth.
Just as fire burns a heap of cotton, so does the water of the Gaṅgā burn away everything;
all merit is found in the Kṛta Yuga, while Puṣkara is remembered as the preeminent place in the Tretā Yuga.
Kurukṣetra is remembered as the best in the Dvāpara age, the Gaṅgā in the Kali age; one should perform penance at Puṣkara and give gifts during the great dissolution (Mahālaya).
One should purify oneself by entering fire, or by leaping from the Bhṛgutuṅga cliff— both of which lead to destruction—
or by staying at Puṣkara, Kurukṣetra, or in the midst of the waters of the Gaṅgā.

Vasiṣṭha said:

Nārada said:

Ātreya, Kauṇḍinya, Viśvāmitra, Gautama, Asita Devala, Mārkaṇḍeya, and Gālava; ||116||

Just as the righteous-souled Yayāti and King Purūravas,

Just as King Bhagīratha, and as the renowned Rāma,

Sūta said:
Having thus addressed the king, the venerable sage Nārada took leave of the great monarch and vanished right there.
The righteous King Yudhiṣṭhira, firm in his vows, accompanied by the sages,

"O sages, whoever reads or even hears this narrative concerning the undertaking of a pilgrimage to sacred fords (tīrthayātrā) as told by me shall be liberated from all sins. (126)
I have explained the entire truth; what more do you wish to hear?
For me, there is truly nothing that remains unspoken regarding these sages of meritorious fame.

Chapter Forty.
Sūta said:
O you of virtuous vows, thus have been described these sacred fords (tīrthas) which constitute the body of Viṣṇu.
Through detachment from any one of these, a person becomes liberated. ||1||
Blessed is the hearing of accounts of sacred fords, and blessed is the service of sacred fords;

"I shall dwell at the sacred ford; likewise, I shall touch the sacred ford"—he who speaks thus every day attains the supreme, great state. (3)
His sins are destroyed merely by conversing with a holy place;

By the mere service of sacred fords (tīrthas), the Lord Nārāyaṇa, the creator of the world, becomes served; there is no state higher than a sacred ford. ||5||
The Brahmin, the Tulasī plant, the Aśvattha tree, the collection of sacred fords (tīrthas), and Viṣṇu, the Supreme Lord—these alone are always to be served by men. (6)
O best of sages, the foremost of men know that the specific service of Brahmins is superior to bathing in all sacred fords and other such acts. (7)

Therefore, the wise person should daily worship the auspicious feet of the twice-born, which are directly composed of all sacred fords; therein lies a merit greater than that of all other holy places. (8)
One should perform circumambulation of the Aśvattha tree, the Tulasī plant, and cows;
having obtained the fruit of all sacred fords, one is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. ||9||
Therefore, one should destroy the effects of evil deeds by resorting to sacred fords (tīrtha);
otherwise, one goes to hell, for [the suffering] subsides only through the experiencing of the karma.
Sinners dwell in hell, while the virtuous enjoy heaven;
therefore, a wise person should indeed resort to this sacred ford (tīrtha). ||11||
The sages said: "O observer of noble vows, we have heard of various sacred fords (tīrthas) and their greatness;
now we wish to hear about the specific excellence of Prayāga."
"O Sūta, Prayāga was previously mentioned by you in brief;
we wish to hear about it in detail. O son of Sūta, please tell us. (13)
Sūta said:
O highly fortunate ones of excellent vows, you have asked well regarding Prayāga;
I shall indeed relate that description of Prayāga to you.
That which was formerly narrated by Mārkaṇḍeya to the son of Pāṇḍu,
when the Bhārata war had concluded and the son of Pṛthā had obtained the kingdom.
Then, at that time, King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, tormented by grief for his brothers, reflected upon this again and again. (16)
King Duryodhana was the commander of eleven armies; he tormented us in many ways, yet all of us have met our end at his hands. 17.
Having taken refuge in Vāsudeva, the five Pāṇḍavas remain as the sole survivors;

King Duryodhana, along with his brothers and sons, and all the other kings who considered themselves heroes, have been slain. (19)
"What is the use of enjoyments or even life itself without sovereignty?
Thinking thus, "Alas, what misery!", the king fell into a state of agitation.
Then, devoid of movement and lacking all enthusiasm, he remains with his face cast downward;

"By what method, yoga, observance, or even pilgrimage site might I quickly be liberated from the taint of this great sin? (22)

Then they all fell upon the ground, weeping together;

Having arrived at Hastināpura, he stood at the royal gate;

"Desirous of seeing you, that sage Mārkaṇḍa stands at the gate. Then Dharmaputra, acting with haste and intent upon his purpose, approached the door.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:

The high-souled Yudhiṣṭhira then worshipped that sage;

"O King, tell me why you have come in such haste;

Yudhiṣṭhira said:

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

How much more so for a kṣatriya, especially one who acts according to the duty of kingship? Keeping this very point in mind, one should therefore not contemplate evil. (37)
Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, bowing his head to the sage, said:
"O best of sages, you who always perceive the three periods of time, I ask you this."

Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Listen, O King, O highly fortunate descendant of Bharata, to that which you ask me concerning Sāṃkhya,
Yoga, and the sacred ford (tīrtha), O Yudhiṣṭhira.

Thus ends the fortieth chapter in the Svargakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa. ||40||
Chapter Forty-one.
Yudhiṣṭhira said: O Blessed One, I desire to hear how things existed in a former kalpa.
How do men travel to Prayāga, and what is it like there? ||1||
What is the destination of those who die there, and what is the fruit for those who have bathed?
What is the fruit for those who dwell at Prayāga? Please tell me this.
Tell me all of this; I have a great curiosity regarding it.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
"O dear child, I shall tell you that which was desired by you, along with its fruit,

From Prayāga to Pratiṣṭhāna, as far as the lake of Vāsuki, there are the Nāgas Kambala and Aśvatara, along with many other root-bearing serpents. ||4||

One obtains in their entirety all the desires conceived by the mind; then, having gone to Prayāga, which is protected by all the gods. (18)
Living as a celibate student, one should satisfy the ancestors and the gods;

The goddess Yamunā, the daughter of Tapaṇa, renowned throughout the three worlds, that highly fortunate river arrived where [the other] rivers had gathered. ||20||

(43) Chapter Forty-Two.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:

He who, having reached the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, should give up his life,

One remembers that very sacred site (tīrtha), and by remembering it, one goes there—

(42) Chapter Forty-Two.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:

Having gone to Uttarakuru, he rejoices for imperishable time;

Likewise, the nāgas, the siddhas, the suparṇas, and those who move through the sky;

O lord of men, he dwells in the heavenly world together with his ancestors for sixty thousand and sixty hundred years. (36)

O protector of the earth, he shall obtain a hundred daughters resembling Urvaśī and become the enjoyer of hundreds of thousands of cows.
Awakened from sleep by the sound of anklets,

He obtains a hundred women adorned with golden ornaments and shall become a lord of great enjoyments upon the earth as far as the ocean. ||41||
The lord of the earth becomes the ruler of ten thousand villages;

Having enjoyed abundant pleasures, he remembers that sacred ford again;
then, at that beautiful banyan tree, he dwells as a celibate student with his senses subdued. (43)
Having observed the fast and being absorbed in yoga, one shall attain the knowledge of Brahman;

He is honored in the heavenly world for many thousands of crores of years;
then, having fallen from heaven, his karma exhausted, he descends by the force of his remaining destiny.
Born into a family enriched with gold, jewels, and pearls, he was handsome in form;
then, having gone to Bhogavatī, to the north of Vāsuki.
There is the Daśāśvamedhaka Tīrtha there, and another sacred site as well;
