The fruit that a mortal obtains by the gift of ten million elephants and the gift of seventy million [other things] is obtained simply by touching the water from Hari’s feet. (10)
O Brahmins, the merit that an immortal would obtain by giving away the seven islands of the earth together with their crops, one obtains ten times more by touching the water from Viṣṇu’s feet.
Listen, O Brahmin, I shall speak; what more need be said in brief? Having touched the water from Viṣṇu’s feet, even a great sinner goes to the abode of Hari.
Śaunaka said:
O Sūta, out of compassion for me, please tell how, in the past, which living being attained the abode of Hari after merely touching or drinking [the water]. (13)
Sūta said:
O best of the twice-born, in former times, during the Tretā Yuga, there was a brahmin named Pāpin who was called Sudarśana; he would always eat on the day of Janārdana.
He was constantly disparaging the scriptures and always disparaging his vows;
he knew nothing else at all except for his own belly. (15)
O twice-born one, once when his time had come, he met with death;
the messengers of Yama arrived, bound him, and led him to the abode of Yama.
Seeing him, Yamunā’s brother asked his minister in anger: "O Minister, tell me truly and from the very root whether this man has merit or sin. (17)
That brahmin appears to be a great sinner, engaged in cruel deeds. ||18||
Citragupta said:
"Listen to his sin; there is not even an atom's worth of merit.
O Lord, he constantly ate even during the day of Hari. (19)
O King, that lowest of men who eats on the day of the Lord of the Day-lotuses (the Sun) would be eating excrement;
he goes to a terrible hell.
For a hundred manvantaras, this embodied soul shall remain in hell;
thereafter, he will take birth in the womb of a village pig.
Sūta said: O brāhmaṇa, then, by the command of Yama, he was cast into excrement by the terrifying messengers of that king for more than a hundred manvantaras.
Then he was released and became a village pig on earth;
he would have suffered in hell for a long time had he eaten on the day of Hari.
Then, when his time had come, that brahmin passed away and was born again in the womb of a crow; he became one who constantly fed upon excrement.
And on a certain day, O Brahmin, having drunk the water from the feet of Śrī Hari standing at the doorway, he was freed from all sins. ||25||
On that very same day, a single crow fell upon the hunter;
both the bird and the fowler met their death at the hand of time. ||26||
When the auspicious day had arrived, joined by the divine king of swans (the sun),
the crow, having mounted his vehicle, departed for the abode of Hari.
The greatness of the water for washing the feet, which destroys sin, has been told;
whatever sinful man hears this, his sin is destroyed. (28)
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "The Greatness of the Water from the Feet," in the dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka within the Brahma-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
The eighteenth chapter.
Śaunaka said:
"If one who is indeed deluded should perform the act of approaching a woman who should not be approached during the period of birth-impurity (sūtaka)..."
Tell me from the very root: by what means can his purification be achieved? ||1||
Sūta said:
If the best of the twice-born approaches a Caṇḍālī or a Śvapākī,
he should observe three days of fasting and then perform the Prājāpatya penance.
Having shaved his head including the top-knot and having given two cows as a sacrificial fee,
the virtuous twice-born man attains purification by giving a fitting dakṣiṇā.
If a Kṣatriya or a Vaiśya approaches a Caṇḍālī woman,
he should perform the Prājāpatya and Sakṛcchra penances and give two pairs of cows.
O ascetic, a Śūdra who follows a Caṇḍāla woman should give four pairs of cattle and perform the Prājāpatya penance.
If one should approach a mother, or a sister, or even one's own daughter,
or a daughter-in-law, being deluded, one would undergo the same hardships as those who consort with women.
Having performed three Cāndrāyaṇa penances, he should then give away three pairs of cattle;
having shaved his head including the top-knot, he should thereafter drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).

O one whose wealth is austerity, just as [an offering] becomes pure when the fire has been kindled, so too [is he purified] regarding the wives of his father, the best of the twice-born, and likewise his mother’s sister. (8)
If one approaches out of delusion the wife of a guru, a maternal uncle’s wife, a brother’s wife, or a woman born of one's own lineage, one should perform two *prājāpatya* penances.
O Brahmin, by performing three Cāndrāyaṇa penances and giving five pairs of cows as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the brāhmaṇas, one is purified; of this there is no doubt.
The fool who approaches a cow should observe a three-day fast;
by giving a milch-cow and likewise food, he is purified—of this there is no doubt.
O twice-born one, having dragged a prostitute, a she-ass, a sow, a crow, a crane, or a buffalo from the edge of the water and cast them into a mire of cow-dung and water; 12.
One should remain there without food; by three nights alone one becomes purified.
Having shaved one's head including the top-knot, one should fast for three nights.
By remaining in water for one night, he is purified; of this there is no doubt. But when a man, deluded by lust, approaches a Brāhmaṇa woman... (14)
O ascetic, if one performs the Prājāpatya penance, or likewise three Cāndrāyaṇas,
and similarly gives away three cows, he becomes pure indeed.

A twice-born man who has had sexual intercourse with a Brahmin woman should drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) for three nights; he should give two cows as a sacrificial fee, and he shall be purified of that sin without a doubt. 16.
If one should approach a woman who has gone to another [man], he should perform the Sāntapana Kṛcchra penance;
as is a male elephant, so is a woman; therefore, one should avoid her. ||17||
If a man should once have intercourse with a woman outside the caste or one of low birth, he shall perform the Prājāpatya penance; he is purified thereby, without a doubt. (18)
A woman is like a pit of glowing coals and a man is like a jar of clarified butter;
O Brahmin, one should never stand near her.
A woman who causes conception by a paramour and brings about the end of her family must be abandoned in every way by a Brahmin; in that matter, no fault is found.
One should depart from the house of a woman who begs, even abandoning one's own kinsmen;
she is ruined and fallen from her family, and there can be no further association with her. 21.
If a woman, being deluded, should approach another man for the sake of solicitation, she must perform the Prājāpatya penance and thereafter drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). ||22||
O Brahmin, a woman who, out of delusion, has approached another man—even if she is ignorant—becomes purified by giving two cows; of this there is no doubt. (23)
If he should come [to her], she must be abandoned; no fault exists for the people.
If a Brahmin, deluded by lust, should violate a Brahmin woman, he is a fallen one.
If one should eat even a single sesame seed from that [food], one becomes pure; of this there is no doubt. ||24||
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka," in the Brahma-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
Chapter Nineteen. Śaunaka said:
Having unintentionally consumed feces or urine, or having touched liquor again, [what is the penance]?
O twice-born one, listen as I tell you how their purification may come to pass.
O Sage, one should perform two Prājāpatya penances, visit sacred pilgrimage sites,
give the gift of eleven cows along with a bull, and then undergo a shaving of the head including the top-knot.
Having gone to every crossroads, one should likewise perform the Prājāpatya vow;
then one should give two cows and subsequently drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
Having fed Brāhmaṇas, one becomes pure; of this there is no doubt—even if one has knowingly consumed the food or water of a Cāṇḍāla during times of distress.
If any man has eaten [forbidden food], he should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa penance; having shaved his head including the top-knot, he should then drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). ||5||

One, two, three, or four cows should be given to Brahmins respectively; furthermore, one must avoid the food of a Śūdra, the food of those in a birth-impurity period, the food of those whose food is unfit to be eaten, and [polluted] water.
If one eats the remnants of a Śūdra’s meal, whether intentionally or during times of distress,
one should perform two Prājāpatya penances as well as three Cāndrāyaṇas.

Then he should give two cows; the twice-born man should drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), and having offered oblations into the fire and fed many Brahmins, he will certainly become pure.
O twice-born one, if food has been eaten by rats, mongooses, or cats, it becomes pure simply by sprinkling it with water containing sesame seeds and darbha grass; of this there is no doubt.
O Brahmin, a man who eats palāṇḍu, garlic, śigru, alābu, or gṛñjana, even in small quantities, must perform the Cāndrāyaṇa vow.
A Śūdra who is fond of liquor and meat and who follows base occupations—such a Śūdra a Brāhmaṇa should avoid from afar, as he would a dog-cooker (outcaste). ||11||
Those who are devoted to serving the twice-born, who abstain from liquor and meat, and who are intent on giving gifts and their own duties—they should be known as the best among the *vṛṣalas*. 12.
If a Brahmin eats out of ignorance during a period of birth-impurity or death-impurity, he becomes pure by reciting the Gāyatrī ten thousand times.
A Kṣatriya becomes pure with a thousand [applications], a Vaiśya with five thousand, and even a Śūdra, O ascetic, becomes pure with five products of the cow.
If a person of any caste should drink ghee, water, curd, or milk contained in a vessel belonging to a low-caste person,
even unintentionally, he must perform the Prājāpatya vow.
One should give a greater gift, for one who is pure is purified by fire according to the rule;
even for Śūdras there is no fasting, yet they are purified by giving alone. (16)
O twice-born one, a man who has been struck by low-caste persons with sticks and other such implements should undergo a tonsure including the top-knot and observe a fast for a day and night.
One should perform the Prājāpatya vow or the Cāndrāyaṇa vow;
likewise, one should have a shave including the top-knot and then drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). ||18||
Then one should give two cows and offer food and other oblations into the fire;
[one must also atone for] the drinking of liquor in the house, whether done intentionally or even by chance.
If any man should eat the food of such a person, that man must be cast out from his family;
as must one who steals cattle, seeds, or water, or one who cuts down a leaf of the sacred fig tree.
One who has stolen gold shall perform the Prājāpatya Kṛcchra penance;
having shaved his head including the top-knot, he should likewise drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya).
Just as one should offer three cows into the fire according to the prescribed rite, so too, O ascetic, his food and water should be accepted. 22.
One should eat only in the morning for three days, only in the evening for three days, and not at all for three days; this is the Prājāpatya vow.
O Brahmin, having fasted for one night, he should drink cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and water infused with *kuśa* grass for two days.
The Kṛcchra penance known as Sāntapana, taught by the Sage, removes all sins. ||24||
One should eat a single morsel for three days—once in the morning, once in the evening, and once without asking; then one should fast for three days. This is the Atikṛcchra vow.

O twice-born one, he should drink hot water for three days, then hot milk for three days, and then hot ghee for three days; O sage, bathing once daily is known as the *taptakṛcchra*, which removes sin.
Abstaining from food for twelve days is this *kṛcchra* penance, which destroys sin; it is to be known by the name *parāka*, O you whose wealth is austerity, and it is well-known. (27)
One should increase [the morsels] one by one during the bright fortnight and decrease them during the dark fortnight; this gradual reduction of food is known as the Drāyaṇa vow. 28.
A self-controlled Brahmin should eat four morsels in the morning and four when the sun has set; this is remembered as the Śiśukrāyaṇa penance.
A woman who has killed a pumpkin gourd should drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) for three days;
she should give five pumpkins along with gold and a cloth.
O ascetic, his food should be accepted even if it has been withheld. (30)
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, titled "The Dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka," in the Brahma-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
The twentieth chapter.
Śaunaka said: What meritorious deed did he perform, by which he emerged from that ocean of worldly existence?
In the Kali age, those who are devoted to the Son [of God] shall cross over the blind well of darkness. ||1||
Sūta said:
In the month of Kārttika, which is dear to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, one should perform the morning bath;
with a concentrated mind and devotion, one should perform the worship of Rādhā and Dāmodara.
O Brahmin, having abandoned meat and other such things, she who is devoted solely to the service of her husband attains the abode of Śrī Hari known as Goloka, which is very difficult to reach.
She who offers incense and lamps to Rādhā and Dāmodara during the month of Kārtika goes to the abode of Viṣṇu, having cast off all her sins.
Any woman who gives a garment in her home during the month of Kārttika to the Brāhmaṇas for the sake of Rādhā and Dāmodara shall dwell with Śrī Hari for a long time. ||5||
He who offers a fragrant garland adorned with flowers to Rādhā and Dāmodara during the month of Kārtika shall go to the supreme abode of Vaikuṇṭha.
One should indeed offer oblations such as sugar and other sweets with the syllables *gaṃ* and *dhaṃ*;
[by doing so] for Rādhā and Dāmodara, one shall go to the abode of Viṣṇu. (7)
O Brahmin, whatever one gives to a twice-born person during the month of Kārttika for the pleasure of Rādhā-Dāmodara, its merit shall be inexhaustible. (8)
O twice-born one, that woman who, out of devotion, worships Dāmodara during the month of Kārtika,
yet fails to perform the morning and evening rites, shall dwell in hell for a long time.
Sometimes, in her birthplace, she may become a widow in every successive birth;
and even before that, she may become unloved by her husband. (10)
Formerly, in the Tretā Yuga, there was a brahmin named Vṛṣala who brought misfortune;
he was a resident of the Saurāṣṭra country, and his wife was fond of quarreling.
She regards her husband—who gives her food and drink—as no more than grass; she thinks, "This husband is not worthy of me; my master is another man. (12)
Thinking thus, he indeed gave her the leavings; through association with the low, that great fool ate wine and meat. (13)
She should constantly carry out her master's commands, even if they are harsh at will; she should become like a tethering rope for his feet, even if he should suddenly die.
"Once he is dead, I shall enjoy myself as I please"—thus did that fool deliberate in his heart with his paramour at that time. (15)
"O twice-born one, let us go to another country," he made this agreement. That night, while his master was sleeping, the brahmin cut off his neck.
Having cut off her paramour, she too went to that place;
O twice-born one, when the paramour returned, he was devoured by a leopard.
Seeing this, she wept aloud and fell down unconscious;
after a long time, regaining her senses, she lamented piteously in her bewilderment.
Kalipriyā said:
"Having killed my own husband and come to another man,
that paramour of mine was, by fate, devoured by a tiger as he took his place as master."
"What shall I do? Where shall I go? I have been fashioned by the Creator. ||19||
Sūta said:
Then, O Brahmin, when Kalipriyā had returned to her own home,
she gave her face to Lapanasvāmin and spoke.
Kalipriyā said:
"Alas, O Lord! What a most terrible deed has been committed by me! Tell me, O Master, my heart's refuge, to which world shall I go? (21)
I shall indeed carry out your rebuke as you desire, O Lord;
I am well-disposed toward you, for nothing remains hidden from me.
Sūta said:
She bowed at his feet and departed for another city.
Having entered there, that woman saw many Puṇyajanas.
O twice-born one, there at the Narmadā river, Vaiṣṇavas devoted to the ritual bath for vigor were present in the morning,
and women there as well worshipped Rādhā-Dāmodara.
And they performed worship with auspicious sounds, great festivals, perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, various garments, and diverse fruits. ||25||
Seeing them engaged with mouth-perfumes, she, filled with devotion yet possessed of modesty, asked: "Tell me, O women, what is this that you are doing? (26)
The women said:
"O Mother, everything was auspicious for us because we performed the beautiful worship that removes all sins, dedicated to the two most excellent ones, Rādhā and Dāmodara. (27)
The sin accumulated over ten million births has been destroyed, and my home has been attained;
having abandoned meat-offerings and ritual worship, I have failed to observe the day of Hari.
O twice-born one, having met their end on the full moon day, those stainless ones quickly became servants who went to the abode of Yama. (29)
Then, intent on leading her away with leather ropes joined with anger,
Viṣṇu’s messengers arrived with a celestial chariot fashioned of gold.
Wearing forest garlands and bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, they struck with the edges of their discs; the messengers of Yama fled. (31)
Mounted upon a golden celestial chariot joined with royal swans,
she arrived at the abode of Viṣṇu surrounded by them.
Having enjoyed pleasures there for a long time according to his desire, he who performs the worship of Rādhā and Dāmodara in the month of Kārttika [attains this]. 33.
That worship which is free from sin leads to the enchanting realm known as Goloka; whoever hears this with devotion, or a woman who listens with a concentrated mind, [attains that same state].
The sin accumulated over ten million lifetimes is destroyed for that very person. ||34||

Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Greatness of the Worship of Rādhā-Dāmodara," in the Brahmakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka.
The twenty-first chapter.
Śaunaka said:
O Sūta, son of Muni, tell me everything that occurred concerning Uttama.
You should duly explain the procedure for Kārttika along with its specific observances.
Sūta said:
O best of the twice-born, on the full moon day of Āśvina, one should, with a concentrated mind,
undertake the vow of Kārtika until the Udbodhinī festival occurs.
During the day, a wise man should void urine and excrement facing north;
he should remain silent throughout, and at night, he should face south. (3)
O twice-born one, one should perform the ritual discharge of urine and feces in ashes, cow-pens, cremation grounds, or ant-hills; however, one who is observing a vow must never do so.
One should not discharge feces or urine in the most excellent places;
rather, having taken pure earth, one should wash the left hand. (5)
For the sake of purification with water and earth, first [use] twenty [applications];
one at the anus, five on the penis, and likewise ten on the left hand. (6)
Ten [offerings] should be given for both the donor and the recipient; then, with three [offerings] each, one should perform the purification of the mouth and the formal resolve for the ritual bath.
Having meditated upon Dāmodara in his heart, he should then recite this mantra:
"O Janārdana, I shall perform my morning bath during the month of Kārttika. (8)
For the sake of pleasing Dāmodara, [this] sin-destroying [hymn was composed] by Rādhā:
"Obeisance to the lotus-navelled one, to Śrī Kṛṣṇa who reclines upon the waters. (9)
"Salutations to You together with Rādhā; accept this arghya and be gracious to me.
Then, O Brahmin, one should perform the ritual bath and apply the tilaka according to the prescribed rules.
But he who performs any action whatsoever while devoid of the *ūrdhvapuṇḍra*, all that action is fruitless; this which I speak is the truth. (11)
One should not look upon the body of humans that is bereft of the ūrdhvapuṇḍra; having seen it, one should gaze at the sun.
He on whose forehead a bright mark of clay (*urdhvapuṇḍra*) is seen is to be honored, even if he is an outcaste;
he is pure in soul—of this there is no doubt.
But the lowest of men make their upper tuft [of hair] without a gap. ||13||
On their foreheads there was always the mark of a dog's footprint;
having completed the rituals prescribed for the morning time, they worshipped the beloved of Hari.
One should worship with devotion the Brahmin and the sin-destroying Tulasī, having heard the Puranic narrative of Śrī Hari with a steady mind. (15)
Then, with devotion and observance of vows, he should worship that Brahmin according to the prescribed rite;
[he should avoid] another's seat, another's food, another's bed, and another's wife. (16)
One should always avoid these, especially during the month of Kārttika:
fermented gruel, black gram, meat, and honey. (17)
O twice-born one, the observer of the Kārttika vow should always avoid rājamāṣa beans and the like, as well as meat, flour-based foods, and stale rice.
Dhānyamāṣa and masūrī are said to be non-meat; the milk of cows is non-meat; salt produced from the earth is non-meat; and for a Brahmin, the meat of living beings and animals is indeed meat. 19.
All juices purchased from a twice-born man, water situated in a small pond, celibacy during the fourth period of the day, and eating from a leaf-plate; 20.

O tiger among the twice-born, he should perform [these rites], but he must avoid anointing with oil; likewise, he should avoid mushrooms, the nālīka lotus, the hiṅgu plant, the palāṇḍu onion, and the leaf of the pūtika plant.
Garlic, radish, drumstick, as well as the fruit of the *tuṃbikā*, wood-apple, potherb, pumpkin, and food cooked in a bell-metal vessel; ||22||

One observing the Kārttika vow should avoid food cooked twice, food from a woman who has recently given birth, fish, a menstruating woman, and sexual intercourse with women two or three times [a day]. (23)
A householder or a brahmin should always avoid the *dhātrī* fruit; by eating *kūṣmāṇḍa*, there will be loss of wealth, and by eating *bṛhatī*, one shall not remember Hari. (24)

There shall be an increase in boils on the *paṭola* tree and a loss of strength in the *mūlaka*; one becomes marked with blemishes in the *bilva* and is born into the womb of an animal in the *nimbu*. (25)

In the *tāla* fruit there is the destruction of the body; in the *nārikela*, foolishness; it would be equal to eating the flesh of a *tumbī* gourd or a cow; and in the *kalinda* fruit, there would be the sin of killing a cow. (26)
The *śimbī* is said to cause sin; the *pūtikā* is a killer of Brahmins. Through the *vārtākī*, there shall be the loss of one's son, and through the *māṣaka*, one becomes chronically ill. (27)
There is great sin in eating meat; one should avoid it on the first lunar day (pratipad) and other such days.
O twice-born, he who avoids food for a certain period for the pleasure of Śrī Hari is a true ascetic.
Furthermore, O Brahmin, having given land to that man who observes the Kārtika vow and acts according to the injunctions, you should offer him a meal. (29)
Seeing them, the messengers of Yama fled like elephants;
a hundred sacrifices are equal to a single excellent vow of Viṣṇu, O Brahmin. (30)

Having performed the ritual, the observer of the Kārttika vow shall go to heaven or Vaikuṇṭha; likewise, he destroys any evil deed born of the mind, speech, or body committed against a mendicant or a brāhmaṇa.
Upon seeing one who observes the Kārttika vow, [evil] perishes in an instant;
even the four-faced Brahmā himself cannot measure the merit of one who observes the Kārttika vow.
One would not be able to describe the state of those who perform the prescribed vows, by doing which all impurity departs in the ten directions toward the brahmins. (33)
"O twice-born one, where have we gone and where have we stayed, due to our vow of Kārttika? On the full moon day, according to our ability, [we gave] food, clothing, and so forth. (34)
For the pleasure of Śrī Hari, the observer of the vow should indeed give gifts and also feed Brāhmaṇas;
at night, he should perform a vigil with dancing, singing, and other such activities.
Whoever hears this with devotion, their sin is destroyed.
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter in the Brahma-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka. ||21||
The twenty-second chapter.
Śaunaka said:
O Omniscient One, tell us the majesty that destroys the sins of those who hear it.
Out of incomparable compassion for the welfare and benefit of all living beings. ||1||
Sūta said: O twice-born one, the messengers of Yama do not come to that house where a grove stands in the vicinity of Tulasī, for it possesses the very nature of a sacred pilgrimage site (tīrtha).
O Brahmin, the auspicious grove of Tulasī removes all sins;
those excellent men who plant it shall behold the Son of the Sun (Viṣṇu).
O best of the twice-born, whoever performs its planting, protection, service, viewing, or touching, all their sins shall be destroyed. (4)
Those of noble disposition who worship Hari with tender tulasī leaves do not go to the abode of Death, O Brahmin.
The Ganges and other preeminent rivers, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and Maheśvara,
along with the gods and sacred fords such as Puṣkara, all abide within a leaf of Tulasī.
The sinner who departs this life while joined with Tulasī leaves becomes one who goes to the abode of Viṣṇu; this which I have spoken is the truth. (7)
A person smeared with the clay of the Tulasī plant, even if joined with hundreds of sins, shall,
upon giving up his life-breaths, go to the abode of Hari.
If a man wears the sandalwood paste from a Tulasi twig,
sin shall not touch his body, and he goes to the supreme abode.
He who wears a garland of Tulasī wood around his neck,
even if he is impure or lacks proper conduct, shall reach the abode of Hari through devotion.
He on whose body is seen a garland made of dhātrī fruits or one produced from tulasī wood is indeed a devotee of the Lord (bhāgavata). 11.
He who wears around his neck a garland made of Tulasī leaves, especially one that has been offered as the remains of Viṣṇu’s meal, is worthy of being saluted by the inhabitants of heaven.
Furthermore, whoever worships Janārdana while wearing a garland of tulasī around his neck obtains the merit of ten thousand cows for every single flower. (13)
Those rationalists of evil intellect who do not wear the garland do not return from hell, being consumed by the fire of Hari’s wrath. (14)
One should not abandon a garland of *tulasī*, especially a garland of *dhātrī* fruits, which destroys great sins and bestows virtue, desire, and wealth. (15)
In the Kali age, for as many hairs as the garland of Dhātrī fruits touches the bodies of men,
for that many thousands of years shall they dwell in the abode of Keśava.
Having offered a garland made from tulasī wood to Keśava, that man who wears it with devotion—indeed, for him there is no sin. (17)
Upon seeing a garland made of Tulasī wood, the messengers of the King of the Dead flee far away, like a leaf blown by the wind.
O best of the twice-born, when that most excellent man offers the funeral cake (piṇḍa) in the shade of a Tulasī, an Āmra, or a Dhātrī tree, his ancestors attain liberation.
O twice-born one, he who wears the dhātrī fruit upon his hands, head, throat, ears, and mouth, should be known as Hari himself. (20)
O twice-born one, a brahmin should worship Śrī Hari with dhātrī leaves and fruits;
by worshipping Him even once, the sin accumulated over ten million births is destroyed. (21)
O twice-born one, in the month of Kārtika, the gods, sages, and sacred fords always take refuge in the Dhātrī tree and remain there.
The man who gathers the leaves of the Dhātrī tree on the twelfth day of the month of Kārtika, or the leaves of the Tulasī,
shall go to a hell filled with torment.
Whoever eats food prepared by a Brahmin in the shade of a Dhātrī tree during the month of Kārtika,
his sin arising from the consumption of impure food perishes for the duration of a year.
O Brahmin, he who performs the worship of Hari in the midst of a Tulasī grove or at the root of a Dhātrī tree during the month of Kārtika certainly goes to Vaikuṇṭha.
O best of the twice-born, even water situated at the base of a Tulasī plant,
when taken upon the head with devotion, leads a sinner to the abode of Hari.
He who carries on his head the water dripping from a *tulasī* leaf has bathed in all sacred fords; at the end of his life, he goes to the abode of Hari.
O great sage, in a former age of Dvāpara, there was a certain best of the twice-born;
once, having bathed and offered water with Tulasī, he went home. (28)
Among those named Varcas, Āditya was indeed the most meritorious;
however, a certain eater of food, afflicted by thirst and burdened with great sin, arrived there.
Having drunk the water from the very roots of the Tulasī plant, that swan was struck down;
the hunter named Yaśasimardana also arrived there in haste.

He said: "Did you eat the food and leave after eating it, or did you go away after breaking [the vessel]? Having placed it in an unbaked earthenware pot, you have indeed returned; how can this be endured? (31)
By the command of Yama, the enraged Kiṅkaras arrived with nooses and mallets in their hands to take away those two who were now deprived of life. ||32||
Then, O charming one, having cut the leather noose, Viṣṇukiṅkaras, who had come with cruel intent to bind and lead away the mind, departed.
They quickly helped him mount [the chariot] and, filled with humility, asked:
"O holy ones, by what merit indeed is this man being led away? (34)
They said: "That former king performed very great meritorious deeds;
he constructed certain wells and mountain caves free from disease. (35)
By this, King Aṃhasāra has indeed come to the destruction of Vaiśramaṇa;
there, by the command of Vaiśramaṇa, you have indeed inflicted suffering upon him.
O King, having slept with a woman made of copper, he engaged in dalliance upon a red-hot iron bed; such was his state of distress due to his own past actions.
Then, by the command of Yama, he was made to embrace that heated iron statue, terrifying with its glowing heat;
having done so, O King, he remained there and experienced suffering for a long time.
In another place of torment, he is sprinkled with showers of caustic water; thereafter, in the remainder of his hellish existence, he repeatedly enters wombs of sinful birth.
Having attained birth and experienced suffering for a long time due to one's own karma,
one reaches the abode of Hari by drinking water from the root of a *tulasī* plant.
Now, having heard those words, the messengers departed just as they had come;
along with him, the messengers of Viṣṇu went to the Vaikuṇṭha abode.
O Brahmin, the greatness of the tulasī plant, which destroys sins, has been told;
O Sage, I do not know what might happen for those who perform its service with devotion. 42.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Greatness of Tulasī," in the Brahma-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka. ||22||
The twenty-third chapter.
Śaunaka said:
O Sūta, tell me the majesty of the Sage (Vyāsa), which destroys all impurities.
Out of compassion, even for the remaining five days of the month of Kārttika. ||1||
Sūta said:
Listen, O Śaunaka, to that greatness which destroys sins, which you have asked about;
I shall relate to you the entirety of the majesty of the month of Kārttika and its five days.
O tiger among sages, among all vows, the foremost is the Viṣṇupañcaka;
in that [vow], one who worships Śrī Hari with devotion together with Rādhā.
With perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, garments, and various kinds of fruits, he, freed from all sins, goes to the abode of Viṣṇu. ||4||
Whether one is a student, a householder, a forest-dweller, or an ascetic,
one does not attain the supreme state without performing the fivefold worship of Viṣṇu.
The famous Viṣṇupañcaka is meritorious and removes all sins;
whoever performs a bath there shall obtain the fruit of all sacred fords (tīrthas). ||6||
He who, with a spirit of devotion, offers a lamp filled with ghee before Śrī Hari, in the presence of a brāhmaṇa and near a tulasī plant; ||7||
For the pleasure of Lord Hari, one goes to the abode of Viṣṇu in the sky;
even a sinner goes to the abode of Hari—this truth has been spoken by me. (8)
One should bathe Acyuta with devotion using honey, milk, ghee, and so forth;
then Hari, being pleased, grants fearlessness to that virtuous person.
One should offer supreme rice-pudding (paramānna) as an oblation to the Lord of the Gods;
even the four-faced Brahmā is not able to fully enumerate the merit thereof.
Having worshipped Hṛṣīkeśa on the eleventh day with a concentrated mind, he properly obtains cow dung and attends to it according to the ritual manual.
On the twelfth day, the observer of the vow should consume cow urine as prescribed;
likewise, milk on the thirteenth day, and curd on the fourteenth day. (12)
Having fasted for four days for the sake of purifying one's sins,
and having bathed on this fifth day, one should worship Keśava according to the prescribed rites.
One should feed the Brāhmaṇas with devotion and give them a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā);
thereafter, one should eat only at night, having properly consumed the five products of the cow (pañcagavya). 14.
One who is unable to do so should indeed consume fruits and roots,
or sacrificial food (haviṣya), according to the prescribed rule.
He who performs the five-fold worship of Śrī Hari with tulasī leaves should be known as the Lord Nārāyaṇa himself. 16.
Formerly, in the Tretā Yuga, there was a Śūdra named Daṇḍaka who was devoted to the livelihood of a bandit; he constantly practiced the destruction of righteousness. (17)
One who speaks untruth, betrays friends, is greedy for the amorous dalliances of courtesans, steals the property of Brahmins, is cruel, and is intent on approaching the wives of others; ||18||
I am one who has sought refuge [in you], yet I associate with heretics and outcasts;
I eat beef, drink liquor, and am always a slanderer of others. (19)
O best of the twice-born, having observed that all those kinsmen were betrayers of trust and destroyers of livelihoods,
the brahmin looked upon their house as being likewise wicked.
His kinsmen, having arrived, were enraged at him who was devoted to sin.
The kinsmen said:
"O fool of wicked conduct, you are being led toward your own destruction."
This was acquired by us through unprecedented efforts, within our stainless lineage, without any fixed foundation.
O best of the twice-born, out of anger and also from fear of ill-repute,
they all abandoned that foremost of sinners from their midst with contempt.
Then, having lost all his prosperity, he went to a great forest and,
together with his companions, would constantly engage in the deeds of bandits.
As they were traveling along the road, out of fear that the Brahmin would devour them,
those who were afflicted by hunger reached a certain spot and then departed for another place.
Having entered there, O Brahmin, they all saw many holy people—excellent twice-born Vaiṣṇavas—standing at the foot of the Dhātrī tree. (25)
All these sages departed; that king, who was also a payer of taxes, went to their vicinity and indeed offered them his salutations.
Daṇḍakara said:
"O best of the twice-born, I am afflicted by hunger; my life-breaths will surely depart. Grant me something to eat, for I have come to you for refuge. (27)
Having heard his words, those devoted to dharma were filled with joy, [saying]:
"You are indeed renowned as the 'Five-fold Viṣṇu' (Viṣṇupañcaka), the remover of all sins. (28)
How is it that they eat food on this day of Hari?
Tell me the specific reason for this; you are currently well-informed. (29)
He said: "O Brahmins, I am indeed named Daṇḍakara;
how can my upliftment occur when I am possessed of every sin? (30)
They said, "Perform this most excellent vow, the Viṣṇupañcaka. At the command of the brāhmaṇas, he performed the Viṣṇupañcaka.
Having ascended to the abode of Hari,
which is beyond the reach of death, and having attained the form of Śrī Hari, he remained there, freed from rebirth.
Whoever hears this sin-destroying narrative with devotion, the sins accumulated over ten million births perish for them at that very moment. (33)
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "The Greatness of the Five Names of Viṣṇu," in the Brahma-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, within the dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka.
The twenty-fourth chapter.
Śaunaka said:
O you of great intelligence, best among the learned and knower of the true principles, please speak.
Now, O Sage, [I shall describe] the greatness of my gifts in due order. (1)
Sūta said:
O best of sages, the gift of land is considered the most excellent among all gifts;
by him who has performed this gift, the fruit of all gifts is attained. (2)
O best of the twice-born, he who gives land with its crops to a Brāhmaṇa enjoys happiness in the world of Viṣṇu for as long as the fourteen Indras endure.
Having obtained birth upon the earth as a sovereign emperor,
that king shall enjoy the entire world for a long time and then go to the abode of the illustrious Lord Hari.
He who bestows a piece of land the size of a cow’s hide upon a twice-born man goes to the abode of Hari,
freed from all sins.
Where a hundred cows and one bull stand together— that land, O Tritas,
the great seers declare to be the measure of a cow-hide.
Both the one who points out the land and the one who bestows the land go to heaven by their word;
therefore, wise twice-born men should accept land even while setting aside hundreds of other gifts. (7)
But that ignorant Brahmin who, being deluded, abandons his land, shall become a partaker of extreme suffering in every birth. (8)
O Lord of the World, he who acquires land from another and bestows it upon a twice-born man—to him the Lord grants the supreme abode. 9.
O twice-born one, he who seizes land given by himself or given by another shall go,
together with ten million members of his lineage, to a most terrible hell.
O Sage, for one who indeed seizes land belonging even to a learned brahmin, a deity, or another brahmin,
no atonement is seen even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
O twice-born one, if a king protects land that has been granted by another,
his merit from that act of protection shall indeed be ten million times greater than the merit of the original donor.
O twice-born one, whatever merit is obtained by giving the earth consisting of seven islands,
a mortal shall obtain that same merit by giving a cow to a member of the twice-born.
He who gives a bull to a poor family attains liberation from all sins and goes to the world of Śiva. ||14||
Whoever gives even a sesame-seed’s measure of gold to a brāhmaṇa goes to the abode of Hari, accompanied by ten million members of his lineage.
Whoever should give silver to a virtuous brahmin, a protector of the earth, attains the world of the Moon and shall drink nectar there forever. (16)
O best of the twice-born, he who gives coral, pearls, diamonds, and likewise gems, goes to the heavenly world.
Whatever merit a person obtains through the gift of a tulāpuruṣa, one shall obtain ten million times more by giving a śālagrāma stone. ||18||
Whatever merit one obtains by giving away the earth with its seven islands, along with its mountains, forests, and groves, that same merit indeed belongs to the giver of a Śāligrāma stone. 19.
Whoever indeed gives a Śālagrāma stone to a Brahmin, by him the fourteen worlds are given to the Brahmin.
O best of the twice-born, for him who performs the tulāpuruṣa gift,
there is no further rebirth in the womb of a mother.
The man who gives the daughter of an eminent brahmin in marriage to a śāla-kāra shall go to the abode of Brahmā; for him, there is no further rebirth. ||22||
For the seller of a daughter, there is no escape from hell;
for the giver of a daughter in marriage, there is no returning again from heaven. (23)
He who gives sandals and an umbrella to a twice-born man goes to the city of Indra after death and shall dwell there for four kalpas.
He who gives divine clothing to a virtuous brahmin shall remain for a long time in heaven, wearing celestial raiment, O best of the twice-born. (25)
O twice-born one, he who gives away an old cow or worn-out clothing, as well as one who approaches a young maiden who has reached puberty, likewise goes to hell. (26)
O Brahmin, a wise man should not look upon the sale of a daughter;
even if he should see it, whether intentionally or through ignorance, he should perform the rite of beholding the Sun.
O best of the twice-born, the giver of fruit shall go to heaven free from disease;
there he enjoys for thousands of kalpas a fruit that is like nectar.
O twice-born one, that mortal who offers leafy vegetables to Śiva goes to his abode and enjoys for two kalpas the milk-rice (pāyasa) that is difficult even for the gods to obtain. (29)
Having gone to the abode of Viṣṇu, he partakes of the drinking of nectar, [offering] ghee, curd, buttermilk, and likewise milk. ||30||
One who offers *gaṃdha* and *puṣpa* goes to the immortal abode of the gods;
adorned with *gaṃdha* and *puṣpa*, he shall remain there for thousands of yugas.
He who gives a bed, the essence of gifts, to a brahmin,
goes to the abode of Brahmā and lies there for a long time upon a couch.
The giver of a seat and the giver of a lamp is freed from all evil deeds;
seated upon a lion-throne in heaven, he shall dwell surrounded by rows of blazing lamps. (33)
The man who offers that betel-roll enjoys the entire earth in happiness;
having gone to heaven, he indeed eats that betel-roll while sleeping in the lap of celestial nymphs.
The supreme man who bestows the gift of knowledge performs the most excellent of gifts;
having passed away, he shall dwell in the presence of Viṣṇu for as many ages as there are syllables in that [gift]. (35)
O best of the twice-born, the knowledge to be attained there is difficult to obtain;
O twice-born one, by the grace of Śrī Hari, one attains that difficult-to-attain liberation. (36)
The best of men should cause a helpless and suffering brāhmaṇa to recite [the scripture];
he goes to the abode of Śrī Hari, freed from rebirth. ||37||
If a person, endowed with devotion and faith, should give a book,
he would obtain for every single syllable the merit born from the gift of ten million tawny cows.
The giver of honey goes to the world of the Apsarases; the giver of molasses, to the world of the Maruts;
and the giver of salt, to the world of Varuṇa. (39)
O best of the twice-born, among all gifts, food and water have been proclaimed by all the sages who know reality to be the most excellent. (40)
O best of the twice-born, by giving food to the foremost of brahmins on this earth, one has effectively given all possible gifts. 41.
A man who gives food is proclaimed to be a giver of life to the Brahmins;
therefore, among all gifts, he obtains the fruit of the gift of food. 42.
Just as food is, so too is water declared to be its equal;
for without water, O best of the twice-born, food cannot be prepared. (43)
Hunger and thirst are proclaimed to be equal to tigers and snakes; therefore, food and water are said by the wise to be the most excellent [remedies]. (44)
O Brahman, those best of men who perform the gift of food on earth, being liberated from all sins, go to the abode of Hari. 45.
O ascetic, as many grains as he bestows upon the circle of the earth, so many sins of killing a Brahmin are surely destroyed. 46.
O Śaunaka, those who bestow gifts of food and bodies cast off their sins; having abandoned them, they suddenly depart, leaving behind only the limbs that were grasped. 47.
Therefore, the wise do not accept food from the most sinful;
those fools who accept it out of delusion become partakers of sin. 48.
O best of the twice-born, one should perform even a single water-offering upon the ground;
liberated from all sins, he shall go to the abode of Hari. 49.
O best of the twice-born, one should diligently accumulate wealth;
and once wealth has been accumulated, O Brahmin, one should disburse it through acts of giving.
Those who, out of miserliness, lament over their wealth are exceedingly miserable;
but those who have renounced all their wealth, O Sage, come here as the truly destitute.
Those men who, having given this gift, become impoverished as if they had not given it at all, should be known as thieves; yet in the world of men, they are like great lords.

In this world devoid of the virtuous—who are like tigers among the twice-born—and which is merciless and lacking in righteousness, that which has not been given does not remain [with one] in the next world. (53)
He who indeed possesses wealth but neither eats nor gives it away should be known as truly poor; having departed from this life, he shall utter a sigh of despair.
Even better than austerity, charity has been proclaimed by those who perceive the truth;
therefore, O best of the twice-born, one should perform the act of giving with great effort. (55)
If a donor does not give a gift to a twice-born man after having promised it, he goes to a terrible hell that brings suffering to all living beings and to himself. (56)
If the giver does not remember having given a gift and the recipient does not ask for it, both shall dwell in hell for as long as the moon and sun endure. (57)
O best of the twice-born, those sins such as the killing of a Brahmin are indeed destroyed by giving;
therefore, one should practice the act of giving.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka," in the Brahma-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa. ||24||
The twenty-fifth chapter.
Śaunaka said:
The life-story of Viṣṇu, which bestows fortune and destroys all calamities.
It brings about the destruction of all evils and wards off malevolent planets. ||1||
It bestows the presence of Viṣṇu and grants the fruits of the four aims of human life;
that man who listens with devotion shall go to the abode of Hari.
The greatness of the utterance of the Name is heard to be most wonderful; by the mere utterance of it, a person shall attain the supreme state. (3)
"Tell me now, O Sūta, the procedure for naming in the *Nāmakīrtana*.
Sūta said: "Listen, O Śaunaka; I shall declare this discourse which is a means to liberation. (4)
Nārada previously questioned Kumāra; I shall relate that to you.
Once, he was seated on the bank of the Yamunā with a tranquil mind. (5)
Having heard various kinds of dharmas as well as contradictions regarding dharma, he questioned Sanatkumāra with his hands joined in añjali.
Śrī Nārada said:
O beloved of the Blessed One, please tell me how the destruction of that violation of dharma by men, which was described by the Blessed One, may come about.
The venerable Sanatkumāra said:
Listen, O Nārada, knower of the dharma of Govinda and beloved of Govinda,
to that which you have asked— the cause of liberation for the world, which is beyond darkness.
Devoid of all proper conduct, deceitful-minded, outcaste, and deceivers of the world; intent on pride, ego, violence, drinking, and backbiting—these sinners are cruel and base. (9)
O twice-born one, even those others who are devoted to wealth, wives, and sons—all such base people indeed become pure by taking refuge in the lotus feet of Śrī Govinda. (10)

We bow down to that supreme elder Devakara, the mine of compassion, who bestows liberation; though he was exceedingly prone to transgressions against other people, he has now attained the eternal state.
Even one who has committed every offense is liberated by taking refuge in Hari;
whereas he who commits offenses against Hari is the worst of men.
The name may sometimes be the cause [of downfall], yet one transcends it by means of the name itself;
for from the offense against the Name, which is the friend of all, one falls downward. (13)

Śrī Nārada said: O best of brāhmaṇas, what are those offenses committed against the Blessed Lord by chanting His name that destroy the religious duties of men and indeed bring them back to the state of material nature? (14)
Śrī Sanatkumāra said: To censure the virtuous is to commit the supreme offense;
for how could one endure the reproach directed at one who has attained renown?

He who perceives with his intellect all the qualities, names, and so forth of the auspicious and glorious Viṣṇu as non-different [from himself], is indeed one who bestows welfare through the name of Hari. 15.

For one who holds the teacher in contempt, reviles the revealed scriptures and the treatises, treats the explanatory passages as mere literalities, or imagines that the Name of Hari is of no avail—no purification exists for such a person through the observance of restraints, nor does he possess the perception that the offenses against the Name are sins. (16)
Neglecting one's religious vows and duties, offering oblations, and so forth—indeed, equanimity toward all virtuous actions—is negligence.
Furthermore, lacking faith, being averse [to the teachings], and not listening to the instruction constitute an offense against the Name of Śiva. (17)
Even having heard the greatness of the Name, that base person who is devoid of love for it, being preoccupied with "I" and "mine," commits an offense against the Name. 18.
Thus, O Nārada, this supreme [teaching] of the sages was spoken by me out of compassion;
it brings happiness to the soul and should always be practiced with effort, avoiding that which belongs to the Lord.
Those who, even after performing sacrifices, avoid the ten offenses against the Name, and who, refusing food even to their angry mother, suffer like children. (19)
O divine sage, one who is free from transgression and always recites your name—by your name alone, everything will be accomplished; not otherwise.
Śrī Nārada said:

How can our offenses toward those who are dear to Sanatkumāra—those who delight in rashness, who are devoid of discrimination and detachment, and who are solely devoted to their own bodies, pleasures, and wealth—be forgiven? 21.
Śrī Sanatkumāra said: Even if one has committed an offense through negligence in some way, one should always chant His name and become solely devoted to Him as one's refuge. 22.
For those who have committed offenses against the Name, the names themselves remove their sin;
for when applied without ceasing, they alone are the means to the goal.
The mere name of Him, whose sign has entered the path of memory or reached the root of the ear—
whether pure or of impure syllables, whether separated by distance or not— is truly that which delivers one across.
O Brahmin, if that [merit] were cast into the midst of heretics through greed born of the body and wealth,
it would not produce fruit here very quickly.
This supreme secret was heard from the ancient mouth of Nārada;
it removes all inauspiciousness and wards off transgressions. (25)
O Nārada, even those men who are intent on committing offenses against Viṣṇu shall attain liberation simply by reciting this name. 26.
The entire majesty of the Name is celebrated in the Purāṇas;
therefore, O bestower of honor, you ought to hear the complete Purāṇa.
O brother, for one who possesses daily faith in listening to the Purāṇas, Śiva and Viṣṇu, along with their attendants, will become directly pleased with him. (28)
Whatever fruit is obtained by bathing at the holy sites of Puṣkara, Prayāga, and the confluence of the Sindhu, that fruit is doubled for one who hears this with faith. (29)
Those who recite the Purāṇas and listen to them with a concentrated mind obtain for every single syllable the fruit born from the gift of a tawny cow.
One who is childless obtains a son; one seeking wealth obtains wealth;
one seeking knowledge obtains knowledge; and one seeking liberation shall attain liberation. ||31||
Those who hear these Purāṇas indeed destroy the web of sins accumulated over ten million births and go to the abode of Hari. (32)
O Sage, one should worship the Brahmin who recites the Purāṇa with a spirit of devotion, using cows, land, gold, garments, incense, flowers, and other offerings. (33)
Filled with joy, he offered a water-vessel fashioned from gold, as well as an earring and a ring made of gold. (34)
O you whose wealth is austerity, one should likewise offer a seat, flowers, and garlands;
for one should not practice stinginess regarding wealth, since a gift given with such parsimony yields diminished fruit. (35)
O Brahmin, one should have the Purāṇa recited for the sake of accomplishing all desires and goals;
[one should offer] gold, silver, clothing, flowers, garlands, and sandalwood paste. (36)
Whoever should devoutly give a book shall go to the abode of Hari;
and those who complete a book according to this rite [shall likewise attain that goal].
O twice-born one, Citragupta records their names based on their worship.
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka," in the Brahma-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
The twenty-sixth chapter.
Śaunaka said:
O wise one, I desire to hear this; tell it to me with its very root.
Skillfulness in fulfilling one's promises, and what fault is there in breaking them? (1)
O Sage, ocean of compassion, having shown mercy, please grant me your right hand; for what could there be that is untrue or false in your word? (2)
Sūta said:
Listen, O tiger among sages, I shall relate this from the very beginning;
for you are the foremost of Vaiṣṇavas, devoted to the welfare of all the worlds. (3)
O twice-born one, the merit obtained by a man who gives a hundred cows is surpassed ten million times over by the merit gained in the fulfillment of a vow.
By the destruction of his own vow, the fool goes to a terrible hell;
he is cooked there for the duration of a hundred manvantaras—of this there is no doubt. (5)
Then, having obtained birth here in the house of a poor man,
one would be destitute of food and clothing and afflicted by suffering due to one's own karma.
One should make an oath by truth in the presence of the gods, fire, and one's guru;
for as long as the lineage of Viṣṇu is not destroyed, it burns the body.
O Brahmin, what shall I say now regarding a false oath?
For one who swears falsely, will there not be a hellish existence for a hundred manvantaras? (8)
O best of sages, having touched or taken the remains of the offerings (nirmālya) of Śrī Hari,
a person is cooked in hell for a long time, even if it be for the sake of truth.
O Brahmin, one who has contracted leprosy in this life may become free from it through truth alone in every future birth; but what can be said of one who speaks falsehood? ||10||
O Kṛṣṇa, that mortal who, having given a gift, protects it, shall attain Him; I tell you the truth, the absolute truth.
As long as a mortal, having given his word, does not fulfill it, the ancestors undergo torment. (12)
Even one who has himself fallen into the most terrible hell shall undoubtedly go to the highest state after death,
being rescued by ten million men.
Śaunaka said:
O sage, tell me how Kṛṣṇa was attained by someone in the past through the observance of a vow; I wish to hear this with great respect. 14.
Sūta said:
Formerly, in a certain city, there was a Śūdra named Vīravikrama;
he was a great eater, possessed of broad limbs, talkative, and exceedingly handsome. (15)
He was wealthy, possessed of sons, refined, learned, and beloved by all people;
he was a worshiper of Brahmins and guests, and a devotee of all the gods. (16)
He was always devoted to his father, the best of the twice-born, and a keeper of his promises; he was an observer of the words of his elders and a servant of Lord Hari. ||17||
Once, a wise young outcaste (śvapaca), having assumed the guise of a Brāhmaṇa, arrived at his house under a pretext and took hold of him. ||18||
The Brāhmaṇa said:
"O immortal one, listen to these wise words of mine; O auspicious lady, out of compassion, tell me now: what shall I do, and where shall I go? (19)
One should arrange a marriage, especially for a Brāhmaṇa; what need is there for gifts, what for pilgrimages, what for sacrifices, or for millions of vows? (20)
Having heard this from the brahmin, Vīravikrama spoke:
"O Brahmin, listen to my words; I have young daughters."
"If you so desire, O Brahmin, I shall give myself according to the prescribed rites;
however, I will not give my right hand, nor will I give myself away in such a manner. (22)
Having heard these words of his, the outcaste, filled with joy, took hold of his right hand and spoke these words: 23.
The Brāhmaṇa said:
"Having given me an inauspicious moment, you have given me a daughter endowed with auspicious qualities;
it is determined in the scriptures that such a marriage will be beset by many obstacles. (24)
Vīravikrama said:
"O Brahmin, I shall give my daughter to you tomorrow; there is no doubt about this.
Yet, that lowest of men who, having given his right hand, should not fulfill it, would be a sinner. (25)
Sūta said:
O sage, having summoned the Brahmin Kṛṣṇaśarman, they told him all this; and he spoke these words to the priest, O twice-born one.
How can you wish to give your daughter to a Śūdra who acts like a Brahmin? Do not give her, especially so, to one who is unknown and of low birth.
O ascetic, all those born of that lineage, Janaka and the others, said:
"O father of heroic prowess, listen to our words. (28)
The family of one whose country, lineage, and wealth are unknown, as well as his character and age, is not given a daughter by her own kinsmen. (29)
He said: "O best of the twice-born, I am by no means able to give the sacrificial fee that you have assigned. (30)
Having spoken thus, he proceeded to give his daughter to them along with the brahmins;
seeing this, all the kinsmen were struck with wonderful amazement. (31)
O Sage, having heard those truthful words, the wielder of the conch, discus, and mace suddenly manifested himself, mounting Garuḍa.
The Blessed Lord said:
Blessed is your lineage, blessed is your dharma, blessed are your mother and father;
blessed are your truthful words, and blessed is your right hand.
Blessed is this action and birth; such as this does not exist even in the three worlds.
O virtuous one, by such action, uplift your family. 34.
Sūta said:
While Śrī Kṛṣṇa was speaking thus, a celestial chariot made of gold arrived,
accompanied by hosts of Hari’s attendants and marked everywhere with the banner of Garuḍa.
O Brahmin, Śaṅkha, the bearer of the lotus himself, placed his entire family— including even the dog-cookers and the family priest— upon the chariot.
Having taken them all, Hari went to the Vaikuṇṭha abode;
there he remained for a long time while they enjoyed that which is very difficult to attain.
He who disregards my word, or he who strikes my right hand, shall go to hell along with his entire lineage; I speak the truth, the absolute truth.
O Brahmin, his food and water are not to be accepted by the ancestors or the gods;
O best of the twice-born, having abandoned dharma, he flees from his home out of fear. (39)
Having granted hope, the fool who then creates despair shall go to hell,
taking with him ten million of his own kinsmen.
He who violates his word violates the Dharma; he is destroyed by kings, fire, and thieves—this truth regarding Brahmins is the absolute certainty of truth. 41.
Having properly heard this *Svargottara*, one shall go to the supreme heaven;
liberated while living, one attains here and hereafter the most excellent abode known as Kṛṣṇa.
Thus ends the fifty-sixth chapter, titled "The Dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka," in the Brahma-khaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa. ||26||
Thus ends the Brahmakhaṇḍa, also known by the name Svargottara.
(Thus ends the fourth section, the Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
Now begins the fifth section, the Pātālakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Salutations to the venerable family deity.
Obeisance to the two lotus feet of the venerable guru.
(1) First Chapter:
The Section on Rāma’s Horse Sacrifice (Rāmāśvamedha-prakaraṇam)
Having paid homage to Nārāyaṇa and to Nara, the most excellent of men, as well as to the goddess Sarasvatī and Vyāsa, one should then utter the word "Victory" (Jaya). ||1||
The sages said:
"O highly fortunate one, we have heard the entire enchanting Svargakhaṇḍa from you;
now, O long-lived one, may we hear from you the life-story of Śrī Rāma. (2)
Sūta said: Then once, Vātsyāyana, the best of sages, questioned the Lord of Serpents, the supporter of the earth, concerning this most pure narrative.

Śrī Vātsyāyana said: From you [I have heard] all remaining stories concerning the creation and dissolution of the universe, as well as the terrestrial sphere, the celestial sphere, and the determination of the circle of luminaries. (4)
O sinless one, you have narrated the distinct determination of the principles (tattvas) for the creation of Mahat-tattva and the others, as well as the various deeds of kings. (5)
The wondrous life-story of the kings born of the solar dynasty is told there, including the account of Rāma’s deeds which removes many great sins. (6)
The account of the horse sacrifice of that hero Rāma has been heard by me from you in brief; I desire it [to be told] in full detail.
She who, when heard, remembered, or spoken, removes great sins;
she who bestows the desired object and grants satisfaction to the hearts of her devotees. (8)
Śeṣa said:
O best of the twice-born, you are blessed, for your mind is thus inclined, longing for the nectar of the pair of feet of the hero of the Raghus. (9)
All the sages declare that association with the virtuous is supreme, because from it arises the story of Raghunātha, which brings about the destruction of sin. (10)
You have bestowed a favor upon me by reminding me once again of Rāma,
whose feet are illuminated by the jewels in the multitude of crowns belonging to gods and demons.
How small is the eye of a mosquito compared to the ocean of the story of Rāvaṇa’s enemy, wherein even the gods, beginning with Brahmā, are deluded and do not perceive it? 12.
Nevertheless, O friend, I must speak to you according to my own ability: birds, relying on their own power, travel through the sky over a vast distance. (13)
The life-story of Raghunātha extends for hundreds of millions of verses;
indeed, according to the nature of their own intellects, people describe it in that very same way.
The virtuous fame of Raghunātha will, through its own contact, make my intellect stainless, just as fire purifies gold. (15)
Sūta said:
Having spoken thus to that best of sages, his eyes steady in meditation,
he beheld with his spiritual knowledge this auspicious and extraordinary narrative.
With a voice faltering and his limbs marked by great joy,
he again related the clear account of the son of Daśaratha.
Śeṣa said: When the Lord of Laṅkā—who caused suffering to the gods and demons, and who robbed the moon-like faces of the throngs of Apsarases of their luster—had been slain; (18)
Then all the gods, headed by Indra, attained happiness;
having attained happiness, they offered praise and bowed down like servants. ||19||
Having established Vibhīṣaṇa, who was devoted to righteousness, in Laṅkā,
Rāma, accompanied by Sītā, ascended the Puṣpaka chariot.
Then Vibhīṣaṇa, accompanied by Sugrīva, Hanumān, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa, as well as his ministers, followed [Rāma], eager for the reunion. ||21||
Beholding Laṅkā with its many broken walls and gateways, and seeing there the Aśoka grove—the place where Sītā was—he fainted. ||22||
There he saw śiṃśapa trees in full bloom with clusters of buds,
crowded with female rākṣasīs who had perished out of fear of Hanumān.
Having thus quickly observed everything, Rāma set out toward the city, accompanied by Brahmā and the other gods in their respective celestial chariots. (24)
Hearing the sounds of the divine drums, which bring delight to the ears, the best of the Raghus was likewise honored by the dances of the apsarases. ||25||
On the way, he showed Sītā the sacred fords and hermitages,
as well as sages, sons of sages, and wives of sages devoted to their husbands.
Accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, he showed him all those places where the wise Rāma had previously made his dwelling.
Demonstrating this very thing to her, Rāma beheld his own city;
furthermore, in its vicinity, he saw the village of Nandigrāma.
In that very place, King Bharata, established in the practice of dharma while protecting the realm, bore many marks of sorrow born from the separation from his brother. (29)
Sleeping in a pit, observing the vow of celibacy, his matted hair bound with bark garments, his slender body emaciated and afflicted by suffering, he repeatedly recounted the stories of Rāma. (30)
He does not eat even a grain of barley, nor does he drink water repeatedly;
having paid homage to the rising sun, he speaks thus: ||31||
O Lord of the gods, the eye of the world, destroy my great misdeed;
for my sake, even Rāmacandra, who is worshiped by the entire world, went to the forest. (32)
He who was attended by Sītā of delicate limbs has gone to the forest—she, Sītā, who used to feel distressed even upon encountering a flower-stalk while reclining on a couch of blossoms. (33)
That Sītā, who even when scorched by the heat of the sun never experienced distress, alas, for my sake that very Janakī now wanders through the forest! 34.
That Sītā who has never before been seen by the eyes of hosts of kings is now surely seen by the Kirātas, who appear like Death itself. (35)
Sītā, who was accustomed to eating sweet food and would never feel hunger, now, while dwelling in the forest, yearns for wild fruits—how strange! (36)
Having thus worshipped the sun every day, he says this morning after morning: "The great king Bharata, the beloved of Rāma. (37)
And when he was being addressed by his wise ministers—who shared equally in his sorrow and joy, who were experts in policy, and proficient in the scriptures—the king spoke to them thus: (38)
"O ministers, why do you speak thus to me, an unfortunate and lowest of men?
On my account, my elder brother Rāma has reached the forest and is suffering. (39)
Constantly remembering the feet of Rāmacandra and my good ministers, I respectfully perform this cleansing of the sins of my wretched self through the power of sleep. 40.
Blessed indeed is Sumitrā, the mother of heroes and beloved by her husband, whose son daily serves at the feet of Rāma. (41)
He beheld that village where Bharata, ever devoted to his brother, was surely staying and lamenting loudly. 42.

Thus ends the first chapter, titled "The Vision of Bharata’s Residence at Nandigrāma by Raghunātha," in the *Rāmāśvamedha* section of the *Pātālakhaṇḍa* within the glorious *Padmapurāṇa*, in the dialogue between Śeṣa and Vātsyāyana. ||1||
(2) Second Chapter. Śeṣa said:
Then, his mind overwhelmed by the longing to see him, Bharata, the foremost of the righteous, was remembered again and again. (1)
And he spoke to the mighty Hanumān, the son of the Wind, dispelling the darkness with the moon-like luster of his gleaming teeth. (2)
Listen, O hero Hanumān, to my words as prompted by your brother—words faltering and overwhelmed by long-standing separation. (3)
Go, O heroic son of the Wind, to your brother, who forcibly bears a body emaciated by separation from me. (4)
He who, afflicted by separation, wears bark garments and maintains matted locks on his head, would not even consume fruits. ||5||
He who regards the wife of another as his own mother, gold as a mere clod of earth,
and protects his subjects like his own sons— he is my kinsman and a knower of Dharma.
Quickly sprinkle with the rain of water from my message regarding my departure that body which has been consumed by the flames of the fire of suffering born of separation from me. (7)
Rāma, accompanied by Sītā and joined by Lakṣmaṇa, along with Sugrīva and the other lords of the monkeys, as well as the Rākṣasas headed by Vibhīṣaṇa—[he saw him thus]. (8)
"Announce that he has arrived comfortably, seated upon the Puṣpaka chariot;
let my younger brother come quickly and happily because of my arrival. (9)
Having heard these words of the wise hero of the Raghus,
the obedient messenger then went to Nandigrāma, the residence of Bharata.
Having gone to Nandigrāma, the wise king beheld Bharata, who was strictly restrained by the elder ministers and deeply distressed by the separation from his brother.
As he was recounting the narrative of Rāmacandra to the elder ministers, he was completely filled with the nectar of the lotus-like feet of that [Lord]. 12.
He paid homage to Bharata, who was indeed Dharma incarnate, fashioned by the Creator from his entire essence of pure goodness. 13.
Seeing him, Bharata quickly rose and, with palms joined in reverence, said, "Welcome! Tell me of Rāma's welfare. (14)
As he was speaking thus, his right arm throbbed;
the sorrow departed from his heart, and his face was filled with tears of joy. (15)
Beholding the king in such a state, the lord of monkeys replied to him:
"Know that Rāma, along with Lakṣmaṇa, has arrived nearby in front of you. (16)
His body sprinkled with the nectar of the message of Rāma’s arrival, he indeed reached a flood of joy; I do not know how many thousands of mouths he possessed. 17.
He said: "There is nothing that I do not give to you;
I am your slave for as long as I live, a messenger carrying the message of Rāma. (18)
Vasiṣṭha, having accepted the water offering, and the elder ministers, filled with great joy,
went toward Rāmacandra by the path shown by Hanumān.
Seeing from afar the charming Rāmacandra approaching, seated in the midst of the Puṣpaka chariot together with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, [he was filled with joy]. (20)
Rāma, too, seeing Bharata approaching on foot, clad in matted hair, bark garments, and a loincloth, [was moved]. (21)
He beheld his ministers, dressed identically to his brothers and wearing matted locks, their forms emaciated by constant austerity. ||22||
Rāma also reflected upon seeing the king in such a state:
"Alas! This is the condition of the wise Daśaratha, the king of kings. (23)
"My son approaches on foot, wearing matted hair and garments of bark;
indeed, O dweller in the forest, no other sorrow such as this exists for me. (24)
"Behold, alas! My brother, my dearest friend, dearer to him than life itself, undergoes such a transformation due to separation from me. (25)
Having heard that I have arrived nearby, Bharata, accompanied by Vasiṣṭha and the joyful elder ministers, is coming to see me. (26)
Speaking thus, the lord of men, having been shown respect by Vibhīṣaṇa, Hanumān, and Lakṣmaṇa, [descended] from the Puṣpaka chariot from the courtyard of the sky.
Descending quickly from the vehicle, his heart moistened by separation, he cried out repeatedly, "Brother! Brother! Again, brother! Brother! Brother! (28)
Having seen this Rāmacandra, accompanied by the gods, safely returned,
the wise Bharata beheld him, his mind overwhelmed by the separation from his brother.
Shedding tears of joy, he prostrated himself like a staff.
Raghunātha, too, seeing him prostrate on the ground like a staff,
raised him up and embraced him with both arms, filled with a light of joy.
Though lifted up forcefully, he did not rise, weeping repeatedly, his arms clinging to the lotus-feet of Rāmacandra. (31)
Bharata said:
O Rāmacandra, O mighty-armed one, O ocean of compassion, show mercy out of kindness toward me, who am ill-behaved, wicked, and sinful. (32)
O Rāma, that very foot of yours which considered the touch of the Videha-born woman’s hand to be cruel, it was that same foot which wandered through the forest for my sake.
Having spoken thus, with a tearful face and dejected, he embraced him again and again;
then, with palms joined in reverence, he stood before him with a countenance overwhelmed by joy.
Raghunātha, that ocean of compassion, embraced his younger brother, and having bowed down and respectfully taken leave of the chief ministers, [departed]. ||35||
Seated upon the Puṣpaka chariot together with his brother Bharata,
Bharata beheld Sītā, the irreproachable wife of his brother.
Did he consider the daughter of Janaka to be like Anasūyā of Atri or Lopāmudrā of the Pot-born Sage?
He thought her to be a devoted wife and bowed down to her. (37)
O Mother, forgive whatever sin has been committed by me, who am lacking in discernment;
for those like you are devoted to their husbands and bring about the welfare of all. (38)
The highly fortunate Jānakī also, having beheld her brother-in-law with respect, greeted him with blessings and then inquired after his well-being. (39)
Having ascended their excellent celestial chariots, they all in an instant beheld from the courtyard of the sky their father’s city nearby. (40)

Thus ends the second chapter, titled "The Vision of Rāma’s Royal Capital," in the dialogue between Śeṣa and Vātsyāyana within the *Rāmāśvamedha* section of the *Pātālakhaṇḍa* of the glorious *Padma Purāṇa*.
(3) The Third Chapter. Śeṣa said:
Having beheld the royal capital where his own people dwell, the wise and heroic Rāma rejoiced, having long yearned for the sight of it. ||1||
Bharata also dispatched his own friend, the minister Sumukha, toward the city for the purpose of preparing the city festival. ||2||
Bharata said:
Let the people quickly prepare for the festival of the arrival of the Lord of the Raghus;
let every house be made beautiful with charming and wonderful decorations.
The royal roads were free of dust, sprinkled with liquid sandalwood paste, strewn with abundant flowers, and crowded with joyful and well-fed people. ||4||
May the monkeys behold their entire courtyards variegated by the luster of banners of diverse colors, like a rainbow at the onset of the rainy season. ||5||
Let them cause incense to be burned in every house of the people,
so that upon seeing its smoke, the peacocks may perform their dance with playful grace.
"Let my elephants, which resemble mountains, be adorned in many ways with red chalk and other mineral pigments, even though they are well-restrained by their drivers. (7)
May the spirited horses, variegated and swift as thought, shine forth even more brilliantly, such that at the mere sight of their speed, even the celestial steeds of Indra feel abashed. (8)
Thousands of beautiful maidens, adorned with all kinds of ornaments and mounted upon elephants, shall scatter pearls. (9)
Let those Brahmin women, with vessels in their hands and holding *dūrvā* grass and turmeric, perform the *nīrājana* ceremony for the great king Rāma. (10)
Distressed by the news of her union with the son of Kausalyā, may she, though exceedingly emaciated and intensely longing for the sight of him, attain joy. 11.
Let the joyful people carry out such arrangements as these, which enhance the beauty of the city, in anticipation of Rāma’s arrival. (12)
Śeṣa said:
Having heard these words, Sumukha, the best among those who know mantras,
then set out for the city to have it adorned with festive arches and auspicious rites.
Then, having gone to that city, the minister named Sumukha proclaimed to the people the great festival of Rāma’s arrival. 14.

Having heard that the Lord of the Raghus had arrived at the city, the people were filled with great joy, even though they had previously abandoned all enjoyments and pleasures due to separation from him. ||15||
Brahmins, perfected in the Vedas, pure and with *darbha* grass in their hands, clad in washed upper garments, went to the illustrious Lord of the Raghus. 16.
Those Kṣatriyas who were most heroic, excellent wielders of bow and arrow, and many times victors in battle—even those heroes went toward him. (17)
The Vaiśyas, prosperous in wealth and with hands adorned with signet rings, dressed in bright white garments, approached the lord of men. (18)
Those Śūdras who were devoted to the twice-born and firmly established in their own conduct, as well as those who were indeed intent on Vedic practice—they too went to the Lord of the City. 19.
Whosoever among the people were engaged in their respective occupations,
each taking his own goods, went forth to King Śrī Rāma.
Thus, at the command of the king, filled with a flood of joy and accompanied by various curiosities, they approached the lord of men. (21)
Śeṣa said:
Raghunātha, surrounded by all the deities mounted upon their respective vehicles,
entered the city of Mohanā with great splendor.
The monkeys, endowed with the power of leaping and traveling through the path of the sky, followed the supreme city with their limbs adorned by their respective splendors. 23.
Quickly descending from the Puṣpaka, Rāma, accompanied by Sītā and surrounded by his retinue, then mounted a chariot drawn by men.
Then he entered Ayodhyā, which was adorned with festive arches, crowded with joyful and well-fed people, and graced by celebrations. ||25||
Resplendent amidst the intense sounding of lutes, small drums, kettledrums, and other musical instruments, he was being praised by bards, chroniclers, and panegyrists. ||26||
Victory, O Rāghava Rāma! Victory, O ornament of the solar dynasty!
Victory, O divine son of Daśaratha; may the leader of the world be victorious! ||27||
Thus he heard the auspicious words of the citizens, whose bodies were thrilled with joy and who were radiant with the bristling of their hair arising from the sight of Rāma. ||28||
He entered the excellent road, adorned with carriage-ways and crossroads, sprinkled with sandalwood water, and strewn with flowers and sprouts. ||29||
Then, certain women of the city, leaning against the openings of their windows, spoke as they were filled with desire born from gazing upon the true form of Raghunātha: ||30||
The city women said:
"Blessed indeed were those Bhillā maidens in the forests who [beheld] the lotus-face of Rāma."
Then, these women, whose great fortune had arisen through their own good luck, drank [him] with the blue lotuses of their own eyes. ||31||
Behold the blessed face of the lotus-eyed Lord Śrī Rāma, the abode of heroes;
even the gods, headed by Brahmā, long for the sight of it.
But we, alas, have attained this through great good fortune! ||32||
Behold this face with its lovely smile, its own head resplendent with a crown,
bestowing a luster that puts the bandhūka flower to shame.
Wearing lip-ornaments and possessing a prominent nose. ||33||

Having spoken thus, those beautiful women gazed upon the world of men— with its full burden of love and its teacher of all things— with glances from eyes resembling lotus petals, heavy with affection.
He, delighted that his limbs were restored, desired to go to his mother's house. ||34||
